It's a very cool update on Gunpoint's mechanics.
*IT IS NOT AN ACTION OR STEALTH GAME* (there is a little of each)
It's a tactical game. You have free movement till combat initiates, at which point everything is turn based. So you've got plenty of time to decide where to jump, what to kill, who to knock through which window...  It's a lot of fun.
Unfortunately, it's eventually let down by the imprecise controls, which are not nearly tight or capable enough to handle things from the fourth level boss on.  It's at that point that you'll die, and die a lot, and worse, only part of the time will it feel like your fault.  But even with that still very worth playing.

Ronin is a game that seems to have aped half the code from Gunpoint and added a single original gimmick. The gimmick is this turn-based combat system that has you jumping around from place to place, trying to avoid gunfire so that you can get up close to stab your enemies with a sword. When it works, it's pretty brilliant. It's a good mechanic, but it lacks polish, and when your one original idea comes with serious bugs, it ruins the entire game. The big issue is that this jumping ballet requires extreme precision, and very tactical thought, as a single mistake will see you dead, and so when the game tells you your jump is going to land you in a certain area, you need to be able to trust with 100% certainty that you will land where expected, else you are likely to die. The problem is that a decent percentage of the time, the game will screw up your trajectory just enough to get you killed, and see you frustratingly replay the same section over and over and over again.
Worse is when the game decides abruptly, and for very little reason, to suddenly drop you out of the turn-based play, and back into real time. If an enemy spots you but you're too far away to attack, they will call in a Lockdown, which can screw up your progress, or cause automatic failure of the level. It takes them 9 turns, or 9 seconds, to initiate the lockdown, giving you 9 turns, or 9 seconds, to reach them and stop them from putting through the call. 9 turns is difficult enough in some of the particularly dangerous levels, where there are a dozen enemies around you, all trying to shoot you dead every turn. When the game suddenly drops you into real-time mode, you can suddenly lose 2-3 seconds before you even realize what's happened, and now you've gone from 8 turns to 5 turns through no fault of your own.
The game can easily be beaten in less than 4 hours, if you're decent at it and the game doesn't screw up repeatedly and cause you to have to replay sections of the game again and again and again. Two sections in particular, which should have been 5 minute sections to beat, took me over 90 minutes to beat because I kept dying. Sometimes it was my own fault, the game can be a challenge even when it's working flawlessly, which is a good thing, but a good chunk of the time I died because the game didn't do what it said it'd do, and got me killed as a result.
Bottom line: The game is reasonably fun, but I'd wait for it to go on a massive sale. Even at the entirely reasonable $10-13 dollar range it just doesn't feel like enough game, and the bugginess can really hurt the fun. If you can get it for $5, and don't mind some frustration, there's a fairly decent game here.

TL;DR This game gets way more negativity than it really deserves. The story is fine and has closure, the characters are pretty good, and the gameplay/world is more refined and interesting than in Human Revolution. Don't like the micro transactions? Ignore them. The ones that come with the game and count persist through multiple saves/playthroughs; the one's that don't trivialize the challenge and are easily found in-game.
If you're concerned about dollar per hour: I played Human Revolution nearly twice with the Missing Link and have a combined playtime of 46 hours; one playthrough of Mankind Divided with the DLC's and, cutting out some fluff time, I've played around 60 hours. It's a pretty great deal for $15.00, and I personally think the DLC's are worth the extra $10.00.
P.S. If you're having trouble running the game, turn off MSAA. going from x2 to off will net you around 20 fps arcross the board and it still looks great.

I was late to the table where this franchise is concerned. I played Batman; Arhkam City nearly two years after its release, and needless to say I was hooked. I wasn't willing to buy a PS3 or Xbox 360 for one game, and I didn't have a PC capable of handling the game, so I had to wait for a while before I got around to this title.
As the title may suggest, Batman; Arkham Asylum (BAA) is a fascinating romp through Gotham's infamous Arkham Asylum. The battle interface used throughout the series makes a very strong debut as you fight hordes of crazed criminals while attempting to regain control of the facility from the Joker. There are several memorable encounters with other well-known characters from the Batman universe along the way. The game very successfully gives the player an opportunity to be the Batman in a variety of situations. One moment you will need to stealthily overtake an area by sneaking through vents and hanging from gargoyles to secure a room full of armed baddies. The next you may be in an all-out brawl with a grundle of thugs. At other times you will use your investigative skills to locate evidence to help you along the way. It is all well done and such a blast! I highly recommend this title to anyone who enjoys a well made game.

O jogo é fo.da demais! Coringa é preso e levado ao Asilo Arkham (nome do jogo), porém não mostra qualquer resistência. Batman, temendo que algo dê errado, resolve acompanhar sua prisão. É quando rola a treta e o jogo começa.
This is a fu.cking awesome game! The Joker is arrested to the Arkham Asylum (the game's name), but didn't show any sign of resistence. Batman think that something isn't correct and decided to check by himself the Joker's arrest. Then a havoc start, and the game begins.
A trilha do jogo é muito boa, os sons são escolhidos em cada momento bem oportuno, ajudando na imersão na estória do jogo. Conta com um total de 212 faixas. Vale a pena conferir.

O jogo em si, por ser uma edição GOTY (jogo do ano), contém poucos bugs, incluí todas as DLCs para o jogo, e uma leve facilitação do mesmo.
É difícil analisar a física do jogo, pois se trata de uma realidade fantasiosa. Contudo, ainda a movimentação dos chefes e da capa do Batman são muito boas (os efeitos de impactos são bem moderados, ocorrendo vez ou outra alguns bugs). A inteligência  artificial é razoável, se um inimigo te ver ele corre atrás de você, se vê um corpo fica em modo alerta e avisa os demais inimigos que passam a te procurar também. Infelizmente (ou felizmente) eles não conseguem olhar para cima durante essas buscas (a menos se você estiver sobre ou muito próximo do corpo).
O game conta com uma campanha principal, com  média de 8h a 10h (27h do meu tempo de jogo foi um bug da steam). A maioria dos secrets não são secretos, o que não estende muito o tempo de jogo. Além da campanha, o jogo conta com alguns Desafios Extras, onde você deve pontuar no caso luta, ou fazer uma missão no modo furtivo, ou fugir do Espantalho em determinado tempo e tals.
The game itself is a GOTY edition, then it has few related bugs, includes all available DLC for the game and it is a little bit easier than the original version.
It is difficult to analyze the physics of the game, because it is a fantasy reality. However, even the movement of bosses and Batman cape are very good (the effects of impacts are very moderate, occurring once in a while some bugs). Artificial Intelligence is reasonable, if an enemy looks to you he runs behind you, if they see a body they be in alert mode and warns other enemies who come to look for you too. Unfortunately (or fortunately) they fail to look up during these searches (unless if you are on or very close to the body).
The game has a main campaign averaging 8h to 10h (27h of my gaming time was a steam of bug). Most secrets are not secret, which does not extend so much the gaming time. In addition to the campaign, the game has a few extras challenges where you must score in fight, or do a mission in stealth mode, or flee the Scarecrow in a given time, etc.
Esse é um ponto muito forte do jogo. O gráfico é incrível, nesse ponto a Rocksteady caprichou bastante. O detalhe de cada movimento da capa do Batman, a ambientação, tudo é muito bem feito, usando muito do recurso até então disponível, que só melhora na obra seguinte.
This is one of the strongest point of the game. The graphics of the game are amazing (in this point, the developer Rocksteady, used very well the sources available to mede the game). Every detail in the movement of Batman cape, the ambiance, simply every thing well done, and the next game in the series get better.

Ingredients
100g plain flour
2 eggs
300ml semi-skimmed milk
1 tbsp sunflower oil or vegetable, plus extra for frying
pinch salt
Method
Blending in the flour: Put the flour and a pinch of salt into a large mixing bowl and make a well in the centre. Crack the eggs into the middle, then pour in about 50ml milk and 1 tbsp oil. Start whisking from the centre, gradually drawing the flour into the eggs, milk and oil. Once all the flour is incorporated, beat until you have a smooth, thick paste. Add a little more milk if it is too stiff to beat.
Finishing the batter: Add a good splash of milk and whisk to loosen the thick batter. While still whisking, pour in a steady stream of the remaining milk. Continue pouring and whisking until you have a batter that is the consistency of slightly thick single cream. Traditionally, people would say to now leave the batter for 30 mins, to allow the starch in the flour to swell, but there’s no need.
Getting the right thickness: Heat the pan over a moderate heat, then wipe it with oiled kitchen paper. Ladle some batter into the pan, tilting the pan to move the mixture around for a thin and even layer. Quickly pour any excess batter into a jug, return the pan to the heat, then leave to cook, undisturbed, for about 30 secs. Pour the excess batter from the jug back into the mixing bowl. If the pan is the right temperature, the pancake should turn golden underneath after about 30 secs and will be ready to turn.
Flipping pancakes: Hold the pan handle, ease a fish slice under the pancake, then quickly lift and flip it over. Make sure the pancake is lying flat against base of the pan with no folds, then cook for another 30 secs before turning out onto a warm plate. Continue with the rest of the batter, serving them as you cook or stack onto a plate. You can freeze the pancakes for 1 month, wrapped in cling film or make them up to a day ahead.

When I saw the trailer for this game, I was very excited. It looked icredibly interesting, and I was excited to explore the levels in their entirety. I loaded up the game, and saw a man in a suit. There were no options or settings, which is unfortunate, but is something that I can live with. Clicking on the man, I was greeted with sad piano music, and a black and white area. To my left, a road, with people walking down it, in the opposite direction that I needed to go. To my right, in front of, and behind me, was an endless void. The music actually picked up, which made absolutely no sense with the colour scheme, and everything else I could see. I tried to interact with something, anything, but nothing worked. I walked down the road, constantly being shoved back by people coming out of... nowhere. I (eventually) reached the other end of the road, and tried to interact with the candy vendor that was there. No cigar. I walked into the building that the (very rude) people were coming out of, and walked inside. Only a single door was labelled, but it was clearly an office building. I could not open any of the doors, and when I walked up to the only labelled door, reading office, I was returned to the menu. The other two "level's" are exactly the same, except even more difficult, starring an old man who is apparently very slidey when he turns, but not when he walks, and a child on the moon. I was lead to believe that this was an exploration game, seeing how people in each stage of life percieve different things and react to them, but none of that is there. You walk in a straight line, and then are returned to the menu. I understand that this is a demo, but the early access description says "then add levels and content later during the development." If the other "levels", if they can be called that, are anything like these three, then this game will be short boring, and confusing, and I will not be playing it.

I went in to this game a little skeptical since I'd never player it at release and the design in some older adventure games has aged poorly. Turns out this is actually the masterpiece that everyone has always said it is, no nostalgia required!
After a short intro the game opens up a dozen rooms that can be explored in the past, present, and future. Most of the items in your inventory can be sent across time periods to solve puzzles, while others are done by taking actions in the past that change the future. It's easy to make forward progress and everything is rewarded with beautiful cartoony animations. The amount of detail in the visuals and audio must have been insanely expensive at the time and is a rare treat.
My biggest gripe is that eventually you'll hit the wall of not being able to make progress with no hint system or obvious direction. Why do you read a boring book to a horse to make it fall asleep? Maybe there's a joke or reference there I'm missing, but it doesn't seem to make any sense without looking it up. It's also annoying, and hopefully not intentional, that the game has 3 different sets of false teeth that could be interchangeable, but are all used for completely different solutions.
The UI overhaul works great and really streamlines problems with the old verb system. And of course you can flip between the old and new at any time to compare.
A bit difficult, and at some times frusturating, it collectively offers a fun expireince that is probably worth your money depending on your personality.

Gameplay feels like a modern/2017 intelligently designed version of Unreal Tournement. Meaning it's not just a rehash of an old game or the mechanics. It's fast, and the mechanics are deep, but it has modern concepts like multiple varied heros, game modes that are more advanced then simple capture the flag or deathmatch, or push the cart, and almost an overwhelming amount of character abilities and mechanics.
For the price I highly recommend it.
The downsides I would say that outside of the gameplay it's still rough around the edges. The game mechanics are deep, very deep, but the tutorial is almost non-existant, so it's trial by fire. You can't choose a game mode to play, quickplay just puts you into random servers that rotate game modes. There's no punishment for leavers, so people just freely leave a game, which will swing the game heavily towards the other team. Lastly, you'll get your teeth kicked in for the first hour or 2 while you learn some of the basic concepts.
Fortunatly, all the rough edges are things that can be changed through updates. The gameplay itself is really solid, which is the important part. If you're even slightly interested in it, and enjoyed old multiplayer shooters (but maybe get bored by them now - like the new quake), this game is worth checking out. It's the right combination of old school feel with modern concepts.
One last thing to add, is that unlike OW (which is a fantastic game, but really does play differently then this) where you live and die by your team/comp, this game lets your skills shine. One person can definitely carry, which is the only thing that ever annoyed me about OW.
The game can be frustrating due to the rough edges, but the gameplay more then makes up for it.

Before I begin this review, it is extremely sad to see people blowing this game off as an Overwatch clone. I've seen reviews of people reviewing the game based off of the BETA VERSIONS and just comparing it to Overwatch with outlandish accusations of copying. No, LawBreakers is in no-way an Overwatch clone. I don't want to beat a dead horse about this, so if you want the reasons why LB isn't OW, look further down in the reviews (feel free to comment on this one if you want my own personal reasons for this, though.)
I love LawBreakers with a passion. In a nutshell, it's the amount of polish, fun gameplay, high speeds of combat and general movement, map design, graphics and developer-to-customer communication (BKP_Brittality on the LawBreakers Discord
is great) which is only the tip-of-the-iceberg of why I love this game.
This game constantly markets itself as a hardcore, skills-only game. While this is true, there are beginner-friendly characters (Enforcer and Vanguard, for example) who can help you get into the game and show of most of the game's true colours. Also, this game gives players MMR/MatchMaking Rating values that queue you with other players of your skill. It is fairly accurate, in my 60+ hour experience of this game. Don't let the marketing scare you away!
I have one minor gripe with the game, though. The marketting team behind this game is failing to promote this game effectively (I've seen like 2 adverts for it since the first few betas) and including the (unjust) OW-comparisons people are making people are branding this game as Dead On Arrival or as "A good game that no-one will play". Furthering this argument makes YOU a part of this problem. Instead of insentivising people to not buy the game because the player count is currently 1k-3k (remember, this game has had very little marketting) does not mean it is dead. Only YOU can help increase the player numbers. Even so, there do exist small yet dedicated communities of games, which this game could end up falling in to.
TLDR: I recommend this game. Look past the player numbers: as long as 10 people are playing, you can matchmake.

Seriously, this game is pretty much a masterpiece.

This game is like no game I have ever dream to play. It's like a life simulator. It has a dark-ish general story and all, like most games, but you get to decide how to get there. I know, I know. You heard that before, right? Well I will honestly say that this game actually achieves that idea in a way where it makes you think about your life and how you want to live it. I dream to make games like this. It takes you on a journey you (Hopefully) won't forget. You get to pick your main character and his/her love interests (which is a great design and makes you connect to your character more). If you like story driven games, this is for you and I suggest giving it a playthrough (If not more, because trust me, you will want to play it again to see if you can get a different ending or maybe make a better choice then you did before). This game will start with a confusing beginning but it'll all make sense at the end. Now this game does have a couple of cons that I have to state at least. This game is heavily driven on text. If you're not a big fan of reading, you might want to stray away from this game. You will not appreciate it all if you can't appreciate the text. Now that being said, I did spot a FEW mistakes in the spelling and some mishaps on pronouns. For the grammar nazis out there, I just laying that out there. But for a game that probably has over 5000 words in it, 1 or 2 mistakes is just being human, or just being sometimes monsters... SORRY! Had to throw that somewhere in there!
To shorten this up though, I'll just make a pros and cons list:
Pros:
+A great story that leaves you thinking about your life
+Choices that make an impact on you
+Humorous at times
+Well designed (for a RPG Maker game)
+Great Characters
Cons:
-Few Spelling/Grammar errors
-My ending made me feel the feels! ♥♥♥♥ you for your feels!

This game satisfies my craving for twitch FPS ala Unreal Tournament and Quake. The Zero G mechanic is fun and exhilarating, reminding me of "6 degrees of freedom" games like Descent and Freespace. Even though the aesthetics are a little generic and uninspired, the core gameplay absolutely outshines that. Each class handles differently, movement and aiming wise. Want to shoot targets from a distance? pick Gunslinger. Want to get up close and personal? Play Assassin or Juggernaut. Movement in this game is an absolute joy to play and master. Even though there is a slight learning curve to it, you'll be soaring through the air and kicking♥♥♥♥♥in no time. Those moments where you are fighting for the blitzball in zero G is like a ballet of chaos and violence. SO MUCH FUN.
The game isn't perfect however, we still need crosshair options, the UI needs polishing, and we have to wait for competitive mode. However none of the cons affect the gameplay at all so the $30 price tag is very reasonable. Also the game runs really well (I'm getting 120 fps on a GTX 1070 at high settings). All in all, I would recommend this game if you're a fan of twitch shooters or getting burnt out with Overwatch. This game satisfies one thing that Overwatch doesn't, which is movement, movement, MOVEMENT.

People that are complaining about preorder bonuses just need to learn how to read.  They got certain exclusive bonuses, and just thought they were getting more exclusives than they were... because they don't read well.  Disregard reviews claiming the dev "lies."
Overall, this game is a lot of fun.  It's refreshingly skill based.  Characters have unique abilities and roles, but none seem drastically overpowered, and there seems to be an effective way to deal with everything by altering tactics.  The emphasis on movement and aiming skill is refreshing, and it's really what makes this game fun and competitive.
The graphics are really nice and shiny with a cool style, and the game is fantastically optimized.  The servers seem fairly well optimized too, and I do not encounter lag except rarely, and ping seems relatively low (I don't even notice any ping).  Nothing like the ping in Overwatch (which may have improved since I stopped playing...but it was really bad from what I remember).
This game is an awesome value for $30, and if you like to get some extra costumes and skins...help the dev make this game greater and long lasting by purchasing the DLC.  Also, there's tons of people playing this game-- I have had no problem finding lobbies full of players, and fast!  It never seems to take longer than a minute to get into a full game!  It's great!

I'm sure whoever worked in this game had high hopes for whatever this game was supposed to be, however, it seemed to fall short of what the concept was supposed to be. I remember this game being touted as "the ultimate vertical shooter", featuring zero-gravity zones that you would traverse by shooting backwards and stuff, which is still there to an extent, but there's little point as only about half of the characters have any sort of survivability in the air. Other characters, like Pharawinston, only have a slam that can either save or kill them, making it have a 50/50 usefulness.
They seemed to want to make the characters have an Overwatch-esque feel, but all of the characters are bland and forgettable, with some spotty voice acting and awful punny names to go along with them. Some characters felt very fun, like assassin, but there's no point in playing them because they die so easily.
The UI looks and feels very dated, reminiscent of a PS2/Xbox era B-Game with it's robotic font and grunge-textured theme. It honestly feels like a lot of placeholder art that was kept in the game.
On top of all of this, the game is $30. $30 gets you FOUR maps and THREE game modes. That's honestly asking way too much for a game that doesn't offer very much in terms of fun, with most of the game modes being confusing, and the only way to see a tutorial is to watch a youtube video embedded into the client, with no actual way to go into a practice room without making a bot room.
Don't buy this game. Don't let the game's cultish subreddit convince you.

This is an incredibly engrossing game.  Even if you don't particularly care for Batman; if you are a gamer - you are going to love this game.  Everything about it is tight.  The story is original and remains true to the motivations of the established characters.  The graphics are beautiful with careful attention to detail taken in every environment and character.  The graphics design overall is perfect.  The sound design is also impressive - from environmental background noises, to the various gadgets, the NPCs, the character voice-acting is superb...  and the music is sublime.  It all just comes together cohesively to make you feel like the vigilante hero Batman, in Gotham city,  tracking down and beating the snot out of the villains of the criminal underworld.   The game contains adult themes and language.  This is not Adam West or George Clooney campy-style Caped Crusader at all.
Gameplay is immaculate with tight, responsive controls.  You play in third person (though there are instances of first person) - Batman can walk, run, crouch, jump, glide, dive, slide, and take cover.  He starts out with a couple of gadgets, such as the grapnel gun, but as the game progresses (and he gains experience levels) he gains some others and the ability to upgrade things like the armor of his suit, the ability to throw more than one batarang at a time, etc...  He has a detective mode which allows you to see things you couldn't otherwise.  For instance, analyzing a chemical in detective mode will allow you to track traces of it in the game.  Detective mode also gives you a sort of x-ray vision so you can see enemies through solid walls to help you form a strategy of how to best approach and deal with a room full of gun-toting enemies.
Batman can kick♥♥♥♥♥ no doubt about it, but many of the enemies carry guns and Batman is not bulletproof - guns will kill him rather quickly.  This leads to part of the stealth aspect of the game (one of my favorite things about the game) - sneaking about and taking enemies out without being noticed.  The variety of techniques in which to engage enemies is noteworthy.  You can sneak up behind an enemy with his back turned and do a silent takedown.  If you're able to sneak up behind two near to each other you can do a double takedown that involves bashing their heads together.  You can grapple onto a gargoyle or something similar and wait for an enemy to pass beneath you - then do an inverted takedown where you string them upside down from that perch.  You can crawl in ventilation shafts and if an enemy is passing near a floor grate you can pop up and take him down with ease.  You can use explosive foam gel to blow weak walls or floors down - and if an enemy is on the other side they will be knocked out of commission.
Taking enemies out via stealth is alot of fun, and true to the character, but it can be very challenging and require a bit of thought and patience.  Many enemies wear a device that sounds an alarm when they are unconscious that draws their buddies to their location.  If they are strung up they will yell for help.  Remaining in the area greatly increases your chances of being found.  Certain actions, such as throwing batarangs repeatedly from the same location will also give you away.  And sometimes, you have to avoid engaging enemies at all, because if you do hostages will die.  In those situations you have to come up with a plan that enables you to both save them and take out the enemies.
When it comes to hand to hand combat, which there is alot of, it's a beat'em up - but not in the traditional sense.  Fighting here is very much a rhythm game - you don't want to act too fast or too slow.  Timing your blows, counters, and such with finesse allows you to keep the combo score rising.  Getting enough combos allow you to do special actions, but as it climbs you enter into free-flow focus mode where you can target enemies farther away and Batman's movements become more fluid, with time slowing to allow for easier target acquisition.  I personally think it's brilliant in it's implementation.  I played using mouse+keyboard, and I had no problems with the combat.  In fact, twice I tried playing with a 360 controller instead, but quickly switched back to mouse+keyboard.
Boss fights are all fun and unique.  And some of them aren't fights in the traditional sense but are more symbollic, even hallucinatory (you'll know what I mean when they happen).  The game contains a number of Batman's most well known enemies, but it also contains cameos from other villains, and data or mentions of still more.  The developers really did everything they could to flesh out the game and give it nuances that make you feel a part of it.
Throughout the game you will also find hidden items and marks left by the Riddler that you will need to collect.  You will also need to solve riddles using clues.  The trophy hunting can get to be a bit much, but many of them require a bit of puzzle-solving, which is fun.  Not only does collecting the trophies and solving the riddles unlock game extras such as concept artwork, trophy models, challenge maps and such, but there is also a story element that makes completing all of this necessary in order to "defeat" the Riddler.
While this game does contain some of the questionable tropes found so often in modern games, they are usually merited, and it also contains some of the best gameplay of any action game I've ever played.  This game is not a walk in the park, as so many games seem to be.  I lost many times in the game, but rarely have I found it more encouraging that I did than I have in this game.  It's challenging without being punishing, and it's rewarding without being coddling.
Simply put:  This is a must buy!

I purchased this game with the expectation it would be similar to need for speed most wanted - Buy a car, Buy upgrade parts, Evade the police, win races, progress the story - that is pretty much what I got.
The reviews here on steam complain about how the car handles & the motion blur effect.
The easist way to solve the car handling problem is to use a controller - some computer games are better suited to a controller while others are better suited to the standard keyboard & mouse. A controller makes it easer to adapt to the way the cars handle.
As for the motion blur - I got used to it fairly quickly. According to google the game was released on November 18, 2008 - which makes it approximately 6 years old as I type this - and If I not mistaken motion blur was a 'feature' of older games used to make thinks look faster. This is speaking from prior experience, from recent memory I have beaten both need for speed most wanted & need for speed carbon (@#$% the final race in carbon) and they had a similar effect when using nitros.
The biggest issue I had with the graphics - I was playing with everything as high as it would go, with the exception of using 1920x1080 due to my screen - and found the lense flair / sun glare to be near blinding. Honestly, more of an annoyance thean anything.
I did also find the music tracks to be somewhat repeative, though I was to lazy to figure out how to turn it off. Something in the options menu I would expect.
I didn't bother with multiplayer, I think the servers were taken down a while ago and I have no idea if this has any other types of multiplayer avalible.
On the subject of the games difficulty - I found the artificial intelligence of the racers to be reasonable, difficult to beat if you are driving an underpowered car and / or didn't understand that you need to turn corners and avoid traffic to win. Yhe police artificial intelligence works well enough, through its nowhere near as effective as what was in need for speed most wanted, and they seemed to be able to keep up with me and even pass me despite driving waht appears to be lower tier cars - I'm guessing thats to give a fighting chane against a human player.
TL;DR
Value: Decent
Graphics: Decent
Audio: Decent
Multiplayer: Maybe Dead
Difficulty: Easy to Medium

The old man bit really got to me.
Obviously I'm not the one to appear all high and mighty, but this game will teach you to care for old people and the disabled. Some of us have been on a train and let the less fortunate/capable stand up for the whole 15/10 minutes of the journey while the train is moving at some 50-80mph. I've had to, on one occasion, tell this guy to give up his seat for this old man who was standing with the support of a walking stick.
While most reviewers have commented how deep/thought-provoking this game is (and they're not wrong), I'd like to point out what this game can possibly be: a sort of lesson in ethics and moral value in everyday life.
For example, in the old man bit, you play as the weak old man, and you realize how difficult it is to cross the road in the middle of a busy city. How many of us realize that the problem is not his weakness, but the people that are driving too fast and carelessly, and the lack of considerations for pedestrians? Personally, if the transportation administration can add this bit of the game as a condition to pass the driving tests, people would be more careful driving in the cities. This can also be applied to the younger peds; in my country, the good manner campaign includes the caring for old people, and as an example (aside from the popular give-up-your-seat-for-the-elderlies bit), we are tought to help them cross busy roads as well.
It also highlights the malleable nature of a kid.
Watching a lot of cartoons showing adventures and action shapes his vision of the world. They also learn from the way people around them act. So if you see a kid acting which ever way, you can guess what he sees a lot, and needs more of.
And there's on more thing this game reminds me to do: while you're still all young and sprightly, go out and do something meaningful to yourself and/or to everyone else, before time comes and grab you by the balls in the form of trembling wrists and weak knees.
+Free (can't charge people money if you want to teach them something useful)
+Minimalist main menu UI very appropriate
+Premise largely expandable in terms of content
+Unique art style in terms of both asset and UI (even as the game progresses further into development, I think the dull and animation-less pedestrian models would still be appropriate in terms of portraying the boring mid-age man life)
+So far, bug-free
+Every aspect appropriately portrays all three classes of characters (controls, visuals, level design)
-Free (if other garbage games can rake in money even with tons of bugs left in development, why shouldn't a brilliant piece like this?)
-Lacks good audio (can really enhance the experience even more)
>Add sounds (faint noises for the old man, dreadful, monotonous BGM for the mid-age guy, and fun-fun-fun BGM/SFX for the kid)

I have heard people calling this game dead on arrival. In a sense that there are not a lot of players that is true. However, this game has had almost no marketing and you will not enjoy the game unless you try it. The reason that people may dislike this game is simply due to one reason. Lack of skill. Gamers will pick this game up expecting to be good from their experience in call of duty and be met with disappointment from someone being better than themselves. The developers made it clear that they wanted to develop a hardcore shooter. Which means the skilled prevail. With almost no RNG slot machine mechanics, this game will teach you two things. How to aim, and how to move. Lacking in either of these areas will lead to another player being more skilled and hence killing you. Its disappointing that some people will run from their fear of not being good enough, instead of putting in time and effort to get good. The top tier players in this game have been playing FPS and hero shooters for years. I have read some of the negative reviews about this game and they all seem to be petty complaints. For example, “Its unbalanced, or other games do this better.” To me these things have no traction for this game. This is a brand-new idea on FPS and class shooters. Mechanics in this game are completely unique and cannot be found in other games. The dynamic behind firefights leaves you craving more action. Please take into consideration that this game is evolving and is not complete. The developers constantly work with top tier players to refine the game and it is because of that the hardcore players from other games like counter-strike, tribes, and quake will find a home here. This game will take time for the player base to form but once it does, it will be one of the strongest in competitive FPS games.

Brawlhalla.
First of all, the graphics in the game are not realistic, but are instead unique and have a cartoon feel. Imagine Overwatch (different but the characters have as much personality as Overwatch) but 2D and £44 cheaper.
A free to play fighting game that has fun gameplay and both local and online functions (which is more than can be said for most other free to play games). With over 30 legends to choose from, there are many different playing styles implimented into the game with several characters to support each one.
The game gives a few free legends each week that it allows you to play. The characters themselves don't cost too much in game money to unlock and so it doesn't feel as pay to win as other games with heroes.
Overall, skill is more important than luck and people that pay to unlock all legends don't have the advantage. There are some times when spamming your signature move will win you a game, but often this simply doesn't work as well as playing skillfully.
Overall, Brawlhalla is well balanced: each legend is able to beat another legend (mostly) and there is not a legend that costs money to buy and inatantly means you'll win. The game as a whole awards player for skill and practice, not luck and spam.
However, there are a few problems: ranked for one. Brawlhalla will often pair me (an awful player with a rank lower than when I started) with a gold or sometimes even diamond level player who has a mammoth coin skin and who will beat me almost instantly and leave me frustratingly cursing at the unfairness. This needs fixing - ranked needs to pair people up based on there rank and not just randomly.
The other is how long it takes to gain gold. The heroes themselves are relatively cheap (with some costing slightly more because they are easier for more experienced players to play - such as Ulgrim, Koji, Wu Shang and Mirage) but the amount of time it takes to get that money is ridiculous. I can spend over 3 hours in game grinding and still be a few thousand off my goal. I know the game is F2P and this technique may encourage people to buy packs (and I think it's good, because the Devs deserve that money for this) but it is frustrating and ruins gameplay sometimes. Since the free heroes rotate each week/update, if you find a hero that you're amazing at and work and train with that hero, you can't buy it easily once the character has left the free rotation - and since that character was the one you were good at, it can be very hard to win battles and so money gaining is even slower than before.
I would quite like to see 5 or so free heroes that stay as free (say Queen Nai, Cassidy, Bodvar, Thatch and Orion) as well as 2 extra free heroes that rotate. In this way, new players can choose one of the constantly free heroes and then gain money to buy the others.
But the game as a whole is a good, fun and unique brawling platformer with a fantastic art style and gameplay.

- Movement is ruined in combat. If hanging in combat there's no way to pull yourself up, you either jump or grappling hook away.
- Button prompts don't show which button to press all the time.
What's the point of Early Access if the final initial release has problems. You're supposed to take feedback and fix any issues before release.

Ronin is an incredible first effort for a one-man project, it allows you to dole out righteous asskickings within an extremely simple framework, the tangible progression in player skill is pure satisfaction. If the game allowed you to play back a level in real time you would probably look like the Primordial God of Ninjas by the time the credits roll.
It's one of the most mechanically creative and solid indie games I've played in years. A brilliant concept that shines confidence and precision in every aspect - the minimal storytelling puts you into the action immediately while still making the stakes clear, the mechanics are deep but don't require much explanation, it knows its limitations and the game ends before it starts asking too much of the player.
Main problem is that around 10% of the time, the controls aren't as reliable as they should be, and can occasionally wig out on you, but outside of the last level the checkpoints are generous enough to where this isn't a dealbreaker. If this guy keeps at it, we're going to be seeing some next-level stuff in the future.

I just finished Ronin and have to say: I'm a stunned!
I'm a big fan of Hotline Miami and Gunpoint, and this was the exact mix of both. The second you realize you can stop time as often as you want as long as nobody has noticed you yet it becomes really awesome. It can be painfully annoying at times to play the same part over and over, especially when the checkpoint requires you to walk a long way rather than just spawning you at the beginning of the battle, but just like Hotline Miami it gives you an overwhelming satisfaction when you've finally finished that hart part you've been playing for an hour.
This is the kind of satisfaction that modern games ceased to give. Nowadays it's all about quick achievement, this game is about doing the same thing over and over until you're doing it perfectly and you're finally feeling like a ninja.
I cannot recommend this game enough.
Pros:
-The ambient feeling is very fitting
-A lot of stealth, but you can also just massacre your way through
-The soundtrack is pretty cool, even if a little repetitive at times
-The gameplay, being a mix of gunpoint and Hotline Miami, is unlike anything I have ever played
-Skilltree you can choose from
-Cool storyline
Cons:
-Not too long, but has a "plus" mode after finishing the game
-Sometimes glitching through the floor ( happened like 3 times in 5 hours of playtime)
-Checkpoints sometimes are at very stupid spots
All in all I'd give this game a 9/10

I love this game, Period. That's all I need to say.
Huh? What's that? you need more than just me saying it's good to persuade you to buy this almost flawless masterpiece? All right then, here I go...
First off, I gotta say the fast pace, hectic gameplay is fun and thrilling. The 0Grav plus the movement system makes you feel like a speed demon of the skies, and the gunplay is amazing. You have sniper-pistols to Rocket Launchers to Grenade Launcher to FRICKIN' LAZERS at your disposal, but each of these weapons are unique to the class you play.
Almost all classes feel different, and the characters, although not as memorable as another team-based FPS that I will not mention to avoid beating a dead horse, are fun and interesting. I would say my favorite characters are Bomchelle, Toska-9, Kintaro, Baron and (my person favorite/waifu material) Sunshine. Each class has a different playstyle, from tanky rocket jumping monsters to sneaky stabby
assassins. Each character is unique and really help build the story of the game.
The story is satisfying enough. From what I can remember, the Moon got nuked to oblivion and Isaac Newton looks like a♥♥♥♥♥♥as gravity is almost non-existant on Earth, and some Criminals, known as "Breakers," are using this to their advantage to steal stuff while the "Law" tries to stop them (which is where the name of the game comes from, if you didn't notice). It's not the most intriguing story, but the Devs have put a good amount of depth in the lore to not feel half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ As said above, the characters really help building the lore and story of the game so it won't add to the cons of the game.
The cons, however, are almost null. I feel that at launch the game is almost at perfect balancing with characters and damage, with only a few exceptions (Harrier's Iron Man Chest Beam just MELTS everyone, and might need a nerf). Other than that, This game is a perfect example of an arena shooter done right.
Though, there is one thing I must address, and that is the very, VERY low playerbase at launch. As it stands, there are usually around 2,000 average players, which isn't a lot, and one of two things will happen: With the help of Twitch they will be able to build a stronger playerbase and achieve the Esport status they want/deserve, OR this game will fade into obscurity, and this gem will be another great game gone dead which I pray will not happen. I've seen it happen with Disc Jam, Evolve, APB, etc., and I hope this game won't add to the list.
But, ultimately, what happens to this game is up to you, the consumer, and with this review I hope will help move you to buy this game and support the Devs. I'm not one to beg, but I implore you, consumer and review reading connoisseur that you buy this game and have as much fun as I do.

This is honestly one of the best games I have ever played and I am generally not all that fond of the simulation game genre. The tension and sense of achievement I experienced with it were quite unlike any other game I have played in over 20 years.
My most memorable moment came when patrolling in the Atlantic off the Western coast of Ireland. According to German command an Allied shipping convoy was expected to pass through the area. I patrolled the area leisurely for days, constantly checking in with my hydrophone operator for signs of the convoy. After 5 days, he finally called out a contact.
I took over the hydrophone myself. He was right. There was the distant sound of screws bearing through the water. I immediately went to consult with my naval charts and try to calculate an approximate course for the convoy and an interception course for my boat. It was nothing more than guesswork facilitated by rulers and sextants. Nevertheless I gave the order for the navigational officer to change course. We had reached the Atlantic uneventfully and still had all of our torpedoes. Anticipation of the hunt crept into my thoughts.
We waited for about a day and a half, following the convoy through the hydrophones. Then the watchman at the conning tower reported he had sighted a ship. I went up in the tower with him and grabbed my binoculars. Distant dots littered the horizon. We had found the convoy. There were a little over a dozen ships guarded by two destroyers from the British Navy. It was late in the afternoon. Night and the protective shroud of darkness were still hours away.
I decided to follow ahead of them and wait for darkness. I returned to my charts and plotted a new course for the navigator. Then we waited. The convoy grew closer and closer. Eventually, sailing on the surface became too risky a proposition and I ordered a dive, still staying ahead of the convoy. As we continued ahead of our prey, daylight eventually gave way to twilight, which gave way to darkness. The moment to strike had finally come.
I ordered every man to battle stations and for the navigator to take the boat off to the right flank of the convoy. The boat was positioned perfectly in the darkness. About 6-700 meters off the closest ship. I ordered the torpedo hatches opened and together with my weapons officer I calculated a firing solution. We were in perfect postition. Our target was a Liberty merchant vessel sailing under the British flag. I fired two torpedoes. They went off towards our target. Due to our proximity we did not have to wait long for the results. Both torpedos scored direct hits and cracked the merchant vessel in two. A fiery explosion briefly turned night into day on the surface. I immediately ordered a dive and submerged beneath the convoy in order to hide the sound of our engines against those of the ships in the convoy and hopefully confound the escorts. It worked.
Throughout the night I hounded the convoy, heading up near the surface to sink another ship before going back down again. I heard the sound of depth charges turning water into foam. I sank 5 ships worth nearly 30,000 tons of shipping. By the night's end we had spent all of our torpedoes and I pulled away, reporting the convoy's position and estimated course back to German command so that other u-boats might fall upon it.
Dawn arrived along with a feeling of euphoria. I set a course back for port. As I watched the sun rise over the Atlantic, Beethoven's "Moonlight Sonata" played from the worn old grammophone in my quarters.
We sailed North and East of Great Britain so that we might stay as far away from British patrols and air coverage as possible. Morale on the boat was excellent. Our patrol had lasted nearly 3 weeks. Then, the Watchman spotted another ship on the horizon. It was a distant, lonely dot. Impossible to make out. We had expended all of our torpedoes in the attack on the convoy, yet our deck gun was still fully loaded and able to sink unarmed merchant vessels. Enthusiastic about my earlier victory and eager to add another kill, I ordered the boat to close in on the distant speck. That was a mistake.
Even as the ship grew larger in my binoculars, I had trouble making out its shape against the horizon. Then, its identity became all too clear, when I spotted two flashes of light from its deck. Panicked, I ordered an emergency dive but it was already too late. The first shell landed in the water a little way's off the boat and sent a geyser of water cascading into the air. The other shell scored a direct hit on the boat.
We dived and I ordered full power to the engines, even as water poured into the boat and started to fill the compartments. The men fought a desperate battle against a tide that seemed to be unending, all the while we descended further and further into the depths... 100 meters... 150 meter... The hull started to creak dangerously. The boat would not pull up. It had taken on too much water. We could not blow the ballast tanks. The destroyer was up there waiting for us...200 meters...
I watched the depth gauge, my heart pounding in my chest. The hull creaked loudly. Finally, the chief engineer had managed to seal the leaks in the engine room and pump out impressive amounts of water. There were dead and wounded. Morale, which had been so high only an hour earlier, was now at a low point. The boat was still going down. I looked at the faces of my men. There was no other choice. Come what way. I ordered them to blow the ballast tanks.
We surfaced. There was no sign of the British warship that had opened fire on us. I could not believe our luck. I immediately ordered the crew to attend to full repairs and for the navigator to set us back on course for home. With luck and God on our side, we managed to limp back to Germany and safety but not without the harshest of lessons.
On the Atlantic Ocean you are only the hunter until you become the prey.

Do you want to sneak through the level without harming a soul? Go for it!
In Mark of the Ninja, you're frail, you can't take many hits. Stealth is your best friend. You can murder from the shadows or stay in the shadows, the choice is yours!

I absolutely LOVE this game.. Yes it takes a bit to get used too.. You have to give it a few hours of actual gameplay and trust me it will grow on you. Each Character has their own skills and abilities and no two classes are alike, some are very tanky and other's are extremely fast and mobile. You can't just main a single character because each toon has it's strength's and weakness's in different game modes. For instance you may pick the Wraith Class or Assassin for Blitz Ball but that same class can get ABSOLUTELY slaughtered in Occupy. Practice different classes and you'll be a great asset to your team.
I'm beyond sick of hearing this compared to Overwatch. The ONLY comparison there is, is the exact thing I just said above, different people with different abilities. Does that make it the same game... Not even close.. Overwatch holds your hand, LawBreakers most DEFF doesn't... LB actually took me a great bit of practice before I felt like was getting better vs OW I was smoking people the first game.. I can't say the same thing at ALL about LawBreakers! This is clearly the OW community trying to protect THEIR game from another game which just might as good, if not better!
In the beginning TRUST me, you're going to get slaughtered. Git Gud and practice and soon enough you'll be breaking the law along with them.
There are multiple modes such as Blitz Ball (Capture the Flag), Turf War (Domination), Uplink (Search and Destroy'ish) Overcharge(Fight over the same battery which holds single charge) and Occupy (All our WAR over a single objective king of the hill type gameplay.. Each mode is great for different reasons but each mode is just different enough to keep you enjoying it thoroughly.
The key to this game is PLAY AS A TEAM! If you're on my team we don't need 3 Wraiths.. 3 Assassins, etc.. I'm the annoying guy that is constantly trying to pump up the team when we're doing well or yelling at people to get in place when all goes to hell.. it's the competitive side in me and I'm sorry! I understand that during BETA play that a lot of people are playing for the very first time and learning so I try and remain calm as possible..
Don't KNOCK this game until you try it.. and I don't mean try it for a couple matches, get smoked and say screw this game and rage quit and go cry on the forum that you asked for a refund.. Get good, Give it a few hours and you'll love it I promise..
This isn't COD, throw your K/D Ratios out the window !! This game FINALLY rewards you for playing as a team and actually playing the OBJECTIVE! IF you have a teamate or two just hanging out in the center of the map you're going to lose.. No joke... You need to WORK TOGETHER as a team to win.. otherwise you will simply be outplayed... Activate your Mic and talk to your team, those are the teams who win..Play the Objective..
Yes the Objective! Imagine that.
You can run/fly around just killing everything but then you're truly missing the POINT of this game..I've seen so many YouTube videos already of my 31/0 and 47/1 gameplay videos... I watch them and I'm instantly bored.. They must be bored as hell too! They're just spawn camping or chilling in the center of the map.. I'm not kidding, go watch one.. Their entire team is running after the ball and you're just hanging out on the other side of the map picking people off at spawn... fun right? I think BossKey needs to add a single shoot them up mode, doesn't matter if it's TDM or FFA, it will help weed out the players who clearly miss the point of these game modes and are useless to a team..
I and MANY others finish with the MVP nearly every match with under 5 kills 90% of the time.. Why?? Because I/we play the OBJ from start to finish.. The people below me could have 20/1 but yet I/WE take first because I played the game the way it was meant to be played!
In OverWatch I only have 1-2 toons that I actually enjoy playing out of the how many? This game I enjoy every single one and love the HUGE amount of customization options, decals, stickers, skins, etc.. I don't need all the lore just yet, keep building this game up with new classes and maps and then worry about the story later..
The playerbase will grow! Trust me! This game is amazingly fun and soon big name streamers will get their hands on it and peole will come rolling in.. WIth the current playerbase I have NEVER waited longer than 30 seconds.. Not once since Alpha! Too be honest sometimes this game starts matches SO fast that I don't even have time to take a drink or get comfortable.
So yeah now GO BUY this game.. It will grow on people and the community with grow along with it, It only takes a few hours before LawBreakers becomes like Crack.. You may have a couple bad matches, get angry, quit and take a break.. then the withdrawals set in! and you're back going at it again that a fat kid loves cake!
Side Note: I have no affiliation to this game. I'm just simply someone who legit loves it and want to see it succeed and played it the RIGHT way as intended...a Hero Team Objective game with the bonus of some bad a** killings. I don't care about your 50-1 game ratio, I want you definding my a** when I grab the blitzball as I would defend yours! Fantastic puzzle game.
It feels involved and direct, as it's all based around movement of your characters (and the charming presentation helps). You're not solving abstract riddles, you're just helping snakebirds eat some fruit.
Despite that, it's incredibly hard, but also entirely fair. Easier levels introduce mechanics that you'll need to solve more difficult levels. For the majority of the game, you'll always have plenty of levels to pick from and try your wits out on, keeping you from feeling completely stuck, and helping you to come up with new ideas for possible solutions to puzzles you previously had no clue how to solve. Also, there's an undo button that can be used freely.
A wonderful side effect of the game is that it was also very relaxing and calming to me. Maybe it was the cheerful music, maybe it was all the snakebirds falling asleep when you wouldn't actively control them, or maybe it was just my poor brain slowly shutting off on the more difficult puzzles. But it was a really great experience playing the game in bed at night, until I couldn't keep my eyes open anymore. Video games as sleep aid. Who would've thought.
(PS: I solved 52 out of the 53 levels by myself, without a walkthrough. I could have totally solved that one level by myself too, if I had just been a little more patient with myself. If you play this, don't make my mistake. Don't spoil yourself. You can totally solve everything in here without any hints.)

Ichi is a solid game build on a simple concept.  It's completely mouse driven, requiring only a number of left-clicks per level.  The first click starts a ball in motion.  This ball will bounce off walls and other objects, such as triangles (which cause right angle direction changes).  Other clicks rotate triangles, or make them disappear or reappear, etc.  Using these principles, your goal is to guide the ball to areas of the 2D level to collect rings.  Early levels have 1 or 2 rings, later levels have more, or are harder to collect.
All the shapes that can be interacted with will do so whenever you click, so where you are pointing does not matter.  In fact, the clicking could have very well been implemented as a keyboard press, though I imagine left-clicking was chosen due to sometimes having to click multiple times quickly.
The levels the game comes with do not take long to progress though, though you will likely replay them at least once to better your score.  There is a grading system based on the number of clicks it took to complete a level.  For example, clearing a level might require 3 clicks in order to get an A, up to 6 clicks gets you a B, and any more than that and you get a C.  In another level, the number of clicks for the A is different.  Your goal then is to get an A in each level, which doesn't take a whole lot of time, and that's fine.
The meat of where I spent my time was creating/sharing my own levels, and then playing those made by others.  This is a cool feature of the game, however, due to the grindy nature of the achievements tied to this feature, (make x levels, play x levels), most people just create crappy levels instead of trying to add to the vibe of the levels that came with the game.  There is a rating system, so that after you play a level, you have the opportunity to give it 1-5 stars and also give it descriptive words such as "easy" or "fast" or even "rubbish".  However, there is no culling of poorly rated levels, nor a way to disclude them from showing up when looking for new user-levels to play.
In the end though, despite the shortcomings of the user-made section of the game, the packaged levels are good, the rating system is not too tough, and the game idea is a solid implementation of a simple concept.  The graphics are minimal, but not in a lazy way.  It comes across as more of a stylistic choice rather than lack of artist situation.
I've talked two friends into also owning this game, so I definitely recommend it, especially when on sale.  I picked it up literally at 90% off, so I definitely got my 49 cents worth.  Whether full price is worth it, is up to you, but I can tell you I've spent $5 on a lot worse things!

Batman Arkham Asylum is an action adventure game that mixes in stealth and a brawler type combo system. It gives a nice variety of gameplay, but doesn’t quite shine on any particular aspect.
The combo system isn’t as fluid as some other brawlers. It is iconic for its ticket system, where each enemy is queued up one at a time to fight Batman. While you can incorporate the full arsenal of Batman’s gadgets, you’ll find most of it relies on your enemies clustering close enough to pull off a large combo. Unfortunately, countering enemy attacks breaks your combo bonus as well.
It also has stealth system which is limited just by line of sight, and sneak attacks. You can’t move corpses around to hide them, and each stealth encounter is limited in a small room with a few pathing options. The other stealth mini-game is a 'red light, green light' game. It plays like a side-scroller, where navigate a linear path avoiding a spotlight.
What bothered me the most was the Bane boss fight mechanic reappearing till the end of the game. While there are a few ways you can approach the fight, it isn't interesting enough to revisit the same fight four to five times.
There’s a detective vision in game, which enable’s Batman ability to investigate hidden clues, and also enables him an x-ray vision to see enemies through walls. This however makes the player rely on this vision too much, as there are no negative effects in leaving it on... Aside from it being visually drab.
Overall, it’s a nice Batman game to zone out on without having to exert too much effort in game progression. But the story and gameplay isn't going to be memoriable.

I would like to start my review off by acknowledging the developers for making the game so detailed and precise as the real world and also including Russian and English as the in-game languages (although it doesn't matter to me, I speak both).
I will write some of the pro's and con's of this realistic first person shooter and outline some key features that the game currently holds.
Pro's: This game has real time bullet ballistics and slow motion if you hit critical shots and feature bullet anatomy if the projectile fired is shattered upon impact of up to 3 enemies or more. The game is focused in a post apocalyptic world with unknown entities such as wild dogs which happen to look mutated, ghost-like in appearance dogs in really big caves and unknown sphere's which zap any breathing or moving object causing instant death or suffocation on the spot. The game also has very nice stealth mechanics which allow you to bypass enemies with ease but if you find yourself in a struggle for life, you can simply unload your chamber of 9mm rounds into the enemy causing internal tissue and muscle bleeding and external entry of bullet (wound). The reloading animation is some what hindered depending on your character's state which could be near death (i.e bitten by dogs or fallen off a certain height) or fully healthy (in which case it would be fast and smooth with no hesitation). You often write notes into your noteback after certain horrific events (i.e Sphere zaps multiple ghost-like dogs). You can read the latest events remembering the horror you bypassed by just clicking TAB which is the default binded key. The game also introduces a new mechanic which is masterbation! It helps with stress levels which your character has and can be increased if horrific anomalies are spotted such as a fat ghost flying across your screen. Of course, you can walk backwards and miss the whole point of this epic game but what boring person would want that?
Con's: This game only features 1 type of weapon which is the standard us military sidearm (The m9 beretta) which was first manufactured in Italy. Although more than 1 weapon would be cool, I don't mind having a sidearm as it's proven as one of the most effective throughout games and history itself.  Also I have a slight complaint about the sensitivity (too fast) but any person can get used to it as long as they use it plenty of times.
Summary: Realistic high quality anatomy,physics and ballistics of bullets and beautiful extraordinary graphics and gameplay, but the downside being the m9 as the only available weapon and slightly overly increased sensitivity.
Over my years of gaming, I have never played a game as detailed and amazing as red lake.
11/10.

It's sad to see LawBreakers stumble out the gate in terms of player population because it's a damn good multiplayer shooter at a killer price point (seriously if the game $60 bucks rather than $30 I'm not quite sure if I'd be that annoyed)

LawBreakers isn't really a pure arena shooter like Quake 3, Reflex or Unreal Tournament but it follows in the footsteps of games like Titanfall that inject a lot of skill based movement mechanics into a contemporary team-based loadout/class formula. The more cynical out there would probably look at this as a defanging of the mythologized idea of the "hardcore arena shooter for REAL gamers", but I think it's better to judge the game as its own thing rather than as the "arena shooter revival" that the game's own advertisements focus on. If you fancy item timers, stack mangement, and a 1v1 duel focus, look elsewhere.

LawBreakers constructs its characters as different schools of thought in approaching movement and combat more than roles/positions to be filled on a team. This design allows for combat to be emergent, dynamic, and fast. Every weapon and ability has an elegant way of being used of multiple different purposes that encourages player creativity. You don't learn how to play a character the best in a single way, you pick them, experiment, and eventually discover a new way of combining their mechanics that may or may not even have been something consciously intended by the developers. It brings the mind the episode of Game Maker's Toolkit where Mark Brown talks about how in the game Downwell, everything from the enemies to the players ability to shoot serves multiple roles, giving the game a lot of mechanical depth without creating too many extraneous mechanics that mostly serve to complicate execution.
LawBreakers isn't perfect mind you. The game is plagued by the same lootbox gambling mechanics that have become worryingly normalized by the gaming industry as of late, and it's aesthetics are..... inoffensive as best, and offputtingly "2edgy" as worst.
LawBreakers is at its best when you have two teams of experienced players going up against each other, allowing the sheer amount of expression the game's combat sandbox enables to take center stage. I can't necessarily say the same about the rest of the game, but it's does this good enought that I'm able to overlook where it either is shallow or simply falls short.

Now to the actual game.
It's difficult... Also refreshing! This game is fast paced and challenging making it all that much more rewarding when you do have your moments of greatness!  Movement is extremely important and only slightly less important to aiming! If you like actual FPS games then this is for you. Everyone is going to compare this to Overwatch. It's really not like Overwatch. Other than they are both FPS games where you have multiple classes. Overwatch is less of a traditional shooter and more of a try to team up and time your Ultimate ability at the right time to swing the tide of battle. I'm not dogging on Overwatch at all! I have hundreds of hours and reached Platinum rankings.  Lawbreakers just requires more of you to be good. Each class has abilities but most aid in movement and another to do damage. No more press Q to win. The skill ceiling is higher and makes for more of an exciting game.
I highly reccomend it! Also only $30.... hard to beat for a game like this.

Straight up, I like this game. I think it's a 7.5/10. Definitely worth playing, but it could have been even better.
Pros are easy to agree with so I'll just put my two cents in on the popular Cons I see in other reviews
"Micro-transactions" - Yep, I hate them too but in my 40ish hours of playing I never once felt the need to buy anything, in fact I don't even know what they're selling since I never needed them or bothered to look. Maybe it had to do with the multiplayer side, I only cared about the single player story.
"Bugs" - Didn't encounter a single bug, I'm shocked to see that complaint show up. Throwing dead bodies with the strength aug is hilarious and completely unrealistic though lol.
"Weak story/just reading emails" - It's a slow detective story, if you think that's weak then so be it. Reading emails and hacking laptops is what this genre of games is all about. However, compared to previous Deus Ex stories where you were a spy/commando James Bond-style character facing off with colorful villains, I can understand people's disappointment with Jensen who's a very by the books cop in this game facing off with some very vanilla terrorists.
"Bad Ending" - I agree, the climax of the game fell pretty flat and made the whole game feel like a prologue to the next Deus Ex game. Which is probably their intention judging by the mid credits cutscene.
"Lack of action/settings" - I also have to agree here, there's only 1 boss fight. I had this arsenal of weapons by the end that I barely touched because the augs and sneaking were so much more effective and rewarding. And it's true, you basically spend the whole game in Prague which is a shame because Golem City was amazing.
So if you liked Human Revolution and you're ok with a story that's slower and doesn't end with a cataclysmic showdown, you'll enjoy it.

So, after a year of alphas, betas, tests and great dev-consumer communication, LawBreakers has finally released.
If you are into any of the classics (Quake, Doom) this game is for you. If you are a modern day FPS fan, this game is also for you.
This game was created from the ground up with passion and shows Boss Key's obvious mastery of coordination, development and Unreal Engine 4. With Gears Of War/Unreal creator Cliff Bleszinski, this game is sure to get the blood pumping. From great visuals to fun and exciting gameplay, this game is sure to be the hit you and your buddies have been waiting for. This game is an absolute blast with buddies and solo players alike, and offers an experience seen nowhere else.
At launch for PC, I have ran into absolutely no issues. As it stands, balancing could use some work, but for a newly launched product, the game, optimization and final product is nothing short of amazing.
With great devs, an awesome $30 price tag and FREE DLC with ONLY COSMETIC CRATES this is sure to be one of the best deals on a shooter to date.
Also, as a side note, thank you BossKey for letting me into each and every test since March of 2016. I have truly seen this game evolve into the fantastic game it is today. Launching this game gives me the early 360 feelings of Gears with my Dad, which were heartfilled memories of the early days.
I also want to stress that this has not set me as bias. What I say in this review is 100% truth.
If you want value, are sick of never being heard as a player, BUY THIS GAME. It's no BS. You are getting beyond your monies worth. It's fun, exciting, competitive and plain out fun for all players.

I really enjoyed the single player experience.
I picked the game up for $30 on sale and I am very happy with my purchase. I've sunk 85 hours into it as of writing this review. I see most of the negative reviews are for the online portion. I wish they had separate store-fronts because the single player is well done.
- Excellent story. I loved it, except there was a few characters that I wish we could of had the option of killing as they were extremely annoying people :P That was by design, so I guess rockstar achieved their goal there. I thought Franklin could of been hashed out a bit more. Trevor definitely stole the show, the guy was hilariously mad crazy. Lots of really funny missions with him.
- Excellent voice acting and characters. All of the voice acting was great.
- Fun and satisfying game-play mechanics. I enjoy all the driving and combat mechanics. Lots of variety in the missions.
-  A small amount of player choice in the direction for major story turning points was fine.

Its so close to being a good game, but the mechanics were not properly refined before release.
Before combat you can do things like jump through the air and with skilled timing deploy a grappling hook at exacting angles, however when combat begins you lose all tactical choice, to a rigid time stopping mechanism.
Ideally something you would want to do is grapple swing through a window, and let go at the right angle to pounce on an enemy. But what happens is the rigid timing mechanism kicks in and you cant let go during the right angle ever.
The grappling hook in general seems like a whole afterthought, it doesn't give you any prediction guides, and often doesn't make sense enough to ever be useful in combat.
You never want to jump, and then grapple to stay in place, since they will shoot you there.
You never want to jump and then grapple in the opposite direction because it never swings you backward (i guess trying to respect the laws of momentum but not in a realistic enough way to be useful)
So I think the only real use of grapple in combat is jumping, and then swinging spiderman style in one direction only.
The fixed time slicing destroys any real tactical possibility in the game. Your jump turns into a white and red arc. The white part is where you will go this "turn"  And you can only shoot your grapple at the exact ending of this turn. The way it should work is you should be able to lengthen or shorten this white area so that you could shoot the grapple at any point during the turn. Even with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ grapple physics, you would at least have some sense of control and more options. The way it is now you have LESS options during combat than free roaming.
There are bugs where you sometimes go through walls, or don't get shot when you should have.
And finally: The way you tackle people mid jump is never consistent so you dont know where you will land or stop moving during the jump.
The end result is not a puzzle, nor tactical, you are just jumping around randomly hoping to get a kill every once in a while.
Instead of actually fixing the game, the developer chose to just put a hint in the game that says "the arc is a lie" ♥♥♥♥ off

It's a game you'll hate playing, but for some reason can't stop playing.
You play as a mysterious heroine who comes straight out of Hotline Miami to avenge her father's work related death by systematically slaughtering his co-workers and countless innocent bodyguards being paid minium wage. Because you know, clearly those people killed your father.
Initially, you'll enjoy yourself leaping from building to building until you realize that the jump controls don't always work and that the enemies you fight against have not only the hacks to shoot through walls, but also the paranoia of Payday's security.
Top it off with the fact that you'll find yourself hopping back and forth as the guards play "Hot Potato" with the Lockdown timer and you soon degrade into nothing more than a ruthless psychopath hellbent on slaughtering anyone in a suit and lab uniform...or who just happens to look like Robo-Cop. Though, your character's sanity is questionable to begin with.
Much like a serial killer, you're poetic enough to stab your rivals up close and personal, and have no qualms with ensuring that every single civilian that holds a gun is immediatley eviscerated into bloody, pixelated ribbons for your sadistic pleasure.
Perfectionists will love this game as there are points where you simply have to remember the approximate random distance to make a jump. Or suffer random spikes where you'll simply hold the pause button in the middle of a machine gun firefight as you realize there's no way out and your luddite of a lunatic is finally getting a dose of modern weaponry from guys who looks like rejects in Robo-Cop.
Of course, if you still get past that, you'll begin questioning the architectural lunacy that makes the most absurd buildings and platforms you've ever seen. Then again, these are the bad guys. You're just the Katana-Crazy Femme Fatale whose had it with being an only child and seeks to reek havoc and drive a motorbike at speeds that'll make even Batman jealous.
All in all though, it's a challenging game and perhaps with more fixes, it can be better.

It combines elements of turn based strategy and action stealth to create something that couldn’t quite stand alone as either. It’s almost unique enough to recommend trying for the sake of playing something different, but its execution is just too poor for me to advise buying it unless steeply discounted.
You're better off buying Gunpoint and/or Mark of the Ninja.
Pros:
+ Solid soundtrack, which fits the tone of the game perfectly
+ Grappling hook can be a lot of fun
+ Despite wearing thin, the idea is still novel.
Cons:
- Tedious. Less strategy and more trial and error as you attempt to find the proper series of leaps.
- Overly simple stealth mechanics which feel inconsistent.
- Repetitive, with no real variation between levels
