Mark of the ninja is a 2D stealth platformer created by Shank creators, Klei Entertainment. To the game's credit the story is more complex than it makes out to be, which leaves the player thinking about their decisions by end of the game. The music does a great job at giving the sense of tension in stealth games.
The gameplay is trully where this game shines. As a ninja you have a vast amount of gadgets available to deal with gaurds such as spike traps, bug swarm, smoke bomb etc. The levels are quite large, generally offering more than one route to reach an objective. Frontal assaults are inefficient at taking out gaurds as it takes alot of hits to knock them down for kill, whille you can die in a few shots. Unlike other stealth games, you can easily see whether your out of site due the the character model changing from coloured (visible) to black (invisible),which means that deaths are hardly the game's fault but rather the player's. There are also alot of places to hide in including rooms, garbage bins and ventilation shafts. The open ended levels and the variety of gadgets allow the player to play their own way (you can even win some levels without killing anyone if your good).
Mark of the Ninja is an excellent game for players who love stealth games with some platforming involved.

Back in the nineties, there was a game called Blood Omen: Legacy of Kain. It felt like Legend of Zelda's grim, klunky younger brother, with vampires and blood, something like if Miamoto was really into Vampire: The Masquerade. It was clunky and had the perfect mix of b-movie charm and over-seriousness, helped immensely by the voice acting. Soul Reaver, basically LoK 2, did the same, albiet more of a Mario by way of Wraith: The Oblivion.
The story started going crazy with Soul Reaver 2, which featured time travel paradoxes, shifting alegiences, and surprisingly good facial acting given one of the major characters has no jaw.
Blood Omen 2, taking place in a time between Blood Omen 1 and Soul Reaver 1, has no real bearing on the either game, and is set up by the events in Defiance, which... well, gets complicated.
Also Nosgoth seems to not count, although it could've taken place befor Soul Reaver 1.
Graphically, it's a solid game. Everything looks like it fits, cinematics are rendered in engine and look dynamic and inspire characterization. Audiably, we have some gloriously hammy voice acting for a very well written game.
Gameplay rewards fighters with special moves, and various magical techniques can make fights straightforward, combined with a brief wait time for dying to keep things from being punishing. At this point in the series, the characters are close superhero levels of power, and the game knows it.
Also, the cardboard tube cheat is hysterical.
All in all, it's a good capstone to a long quiet francise. If this is your entry, you're jumping into the middle of Vampire Soap Opera: the Action Platformer, so you may want to check TV tropes with the spoiler warning on.
And since I bought this outside of steam originally, please disreguard the play time.

I just picked up this game for extremely cheap, and I'm surprised at the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews after playing it. I thought I'd state my criticisms here as food for thought for others considering picking this up.
First the pros. This game is colorful and cute, performs great, and is easy to jump into. The story is not the focus, and it rightly stays out of the way. It's a simple arpg and If you have a buddy to play with, you'll probably have a fun time.
Now the negatives.
Gameplay: I'm only a few hours into this game and it's feeling very tedious already. Gameplay is dead-simple - even on veteran difficulty, I have had no problem progressing through the game with just default click attacks. That's fine in the beginning, but I don't see much indication of increasing difficulty in tandem with increasingly complex gameplay. Potions are cheap and fairly spammable, and the penalty for death is very small, so there is overall a "low-stakes" feeling to gameplay. Playing on hardcore or on the highest difficulty might help, but... eh. Elite enemies way above your level can soak up tons of your attacks and kill you in a couple hits, but even those situations can be resolved by spamming potions and/or kiting. Greater difficulty in this game seems to call for more grinding, more potion spamming, and more cheesy tactics - not more skillful play. I also have to call out the fact that there are a bunch of buffs in this game with 10-60s duration and a shorter cooldown, so there's no reason not to keep them up at all times. This is just tedious as hell.
Character Development: Skill progression is not a tree - skills only have level prereqs - and there are no D2:LoD-style synergies either. So there is not much to think about in terms of builds. With only four classes, I would expect more depth here. Many skills are pretty obviously crap, and some clearly OP, and without the ability to respec (whyyyy), it's clear that you can screw yourself early. To me it appears optimal to maximize leves in one or two active skills, and dump the rest into any helpful passives, notwithstanding picking up a few clear "one-point wonders" (why do these still exist?). But none of this is really necessary - it's not too hard to avoid taking damage altogether by just using normal attacks with a ranged weapon.
I have other complaints: constantly dumping items onto your pet is tedious, fishing is really stupid, gold is ridiculously plentiful, loot systems just isn't that satisfying, "your pet is wounded" every 2 seconds, etc. I'd look into more detailed negative reviews for more. Overall, it's not an awful game, but there just wasn't enough depth or challenge to keep me interested.

I will make this short and to the point.
Storyline: Surprisingly well written considering it could have been another excuse for Batman to hit things. I can say no more (cus spoilers)
Combat: Balanced and rewarding. Combo upgrades take a good few hours to unlock. Dodging five assailants attacking at once and still being able to beat them senseless never gets dull.
Controls: A little unwieldy with mouse and keyboard. It is obvious from the outset this game was designed for consol controllers. If you don't have one hooked up to your PC I would recommend it to get the most from this game. (Remember, with a bit of work you can get your ps3, or Xbox, controller working using the "better ds3" tool and the right drivers if the steam controller looks too pricey)
Graphics: This game has aged well, Would recommend running on highest settings though.
Sound: Atmospheric, no catchy recurring theme music sadly.
Secrets: My personal oppinion is that this game is all about the secrets. I believe there are over 15 for each map area and over 200 overall. It is easy to spend hours (literally) hunting in detective mode for hidden messages and riddle solutions. If you have intense OCD that you wish to placate and cure once and for all with the king of OCD games, then try to get 100% completion on this. No mean feat by any means.
In conclusion... A very solid game which has earned its GOTY title. Expect it to take tens of hours off your life, but not hundreds. The sense that this game IS completable is a very attractive factor.
Would recommend. Enjoy!

So I'm reviewing this to help prespective new players wrap their minds around the whole dash drama. Dash if fine; in fact, it's great. If you didn't know already, for a very long time the only diffensive option was dodge. Initially it was simple, you would get a directional dodge in any direction with a 1 second cooldown on ground and 3 seconds in the air. That was a long time ago. The problem with this was that it gave passive players a much greater advantage over those trying to push in. Any and all approaches were slow and reactable, and you could easily play and win by keeping your distance and solely attack to punish an approach. The neutral game was rather trash. BMG (Blue Mammoth Games) did their best to try an alleviate this issue without massively shuffling mechanics. In the end Dodge became weird and convoluted; If you had enough forward momentum youcould speed dodge, which would be cancelable into an attack, you could dodge again on the ground to extend your current dodge, and you could (and still can, actually) preform an immediate speed dodge after landing an attack. But none of these things really fixed the core issue; all approaches were slow and reactable. So in favor of this new dash, directional dodges on the ground were completely removed; Inputting a direction (left or right) and pressing the dodge key will now preform a dash. This dash can be preformed at any time on the ground and has massive, instant acceleration and speed compared to anyhting else in the game at the time, but you won't have any invincibilty frames. This effectively made unreactable approaches a thing and the neutral game was much faster and intense. However, many people, myself included, had been playing with the old dodge for years now. I personally hadn't had too much of an issue with passive play and kinda felt that dodge was a bit unnecessary. But after having played it with my friends for a bit and then trying to go back to the old dodge, it felt much, much slower. The game as a whole feels much nicer; standing still and waiting for an attack is still a valid thing to do, but it involves more risk than it ever did, and you have to rely on your ability to read your opponent rather than simple reactions to pull it off. It took me anout a week or two to really adapt, and the game as a whole will be much more intuitive for a new player.
TL;DR: People got too comfortable with the old dodge and are now immaturely crying abt it and giving this game bad reviews that it absolutely does not deserve. Please don't let that drive you away from this game. If you ARE one of these people, please look into actually using dash before potenially ruining this game's only marketing source.

Welcome to the Madhouse.
Batman: Arkham Asylum started something extraordinary, from its fantastic combat to redefining superhero video games. As the first game in the series, it is sure to have a few flaws and quite a bit to improve on, which Arkham City does so magnificently, but this still remains to be a fantastic game nonethless.
The game is loosely based off of Arkham Asylum: A Serious House on Serious Earth, by Grant Morrison, and it does great in conveying that dark tone one feels when reading a Dark Knight comic. The story takes its turns here and there and though it gets a little ridiculous and over the top, at least how I felt, it is still very solid. After the Joker takes over Arkham Asylum, he launches a full scale assault on the island and the GCPD protecting it, causing Batman to go on a hunt to uncover what The Joker is truly up to and to stop him.
The combat in this game redefined action games, and though it is improved on in later installments, it still manages to be a very satisfying experience. Other games which have borrowed from this combat style are Sleeping Dogs, The Amazing Spider-Man games, and Middle-Earth: Shadow of Mordor. The game manages to keep the combat interesting by having upgrades for the base system, which is small but feels adequate.
You will face off against a numerous amount of Batman villains that include The Joker, Killer Croc, Poison Ivy, Harley Quinn, Bane, Victor Zsasz, and The Scarecrow. Each of them have their own unique sections, which keeps the game exciting. However, some portions of these unique boss battles got somewhat annoying due to the fact that the PC controls are a bit more troublesome to use than a controller for this game. However, it was not too big of a disturbance for the overall enjoyment of the game.
Now, though the game is great, I do have to say that six years later, it does feel sort of dated so be aware of that if you are meaning to jump into this game anytime soon. That said, the game is still a greatly enjoyable experience and though the story manages to get a little ridiculous at times, the fantastic combat and Batman lore is more than enough to have you invested in the first installment of the Arkham series.

Reading the synopsis for Always Sometimes Monsters I thought it was the coolest thing, since I'm a huge fan of simulation and create your own destiny games. Started out pretty good, and went downhill after about 2 hours.
It just didn't deliver as much as I thought it would. It was tedious, unbelievable, and unsatisfying .
Let's start off with "tedious". To make money, there are various jobs in the game. Jobs like packing meat or tofu into boxes, or sorting weed or other plants into baggies. And let me tell you, they are no fun. Most people know of the infamous packing boxes into a truck scene. You could literally spend about 25 minutes going back and forth putting these boxes into the truck, and if you think "Let's see what happens when I get to 100!" you will be very disappointed, my friend.
For the "unbelievable" part, I just mean that some positions you're put in don't make sense. Really. This game tries to be dramatic and put you in "hazardous" situations, but it just comes off like it's trying too hard. Like it really wants to make your character's life miserable. And you know how this game is basically about you trying to get to your ex's wedding? There's a plot twist (a pretty obvious one) that is totally unbelievable, as in, unrealistic. If you really look at the characters' backgrounds, it doesn't make sense. Seems like it's just there for the sake of having a plot twist.
Now for the unsatisfying ending, no spoilers. Like I said, I love games where the decisions you make affect the story, but in the end, no matter what you do you'll get the bad ending (and that's not a spoiler. You actually start off at the end of the game). I played several times to see all possible different endings, and even when I did everything to get myself the best possible ending, I still ended up homeless. I just don't understand.
Don't get me wrong, I don't regret buying this game. I still play it every now and then. It's got it's perks as a game with a lot of stuff to do and decision to make. I'm just adding some criticism since all the other comments here seem to be pretty positive.
Just saying, expect to get frustrated and question a lot of things.

I've really tried to enjoy this game, specially after reading so many positive reviews about it. I enjoy story based games, and the premise sounded promising enough to catch my attention. But I can't do it, I can't keep going on.
I'll start by saying that I don't mind the graphics, or the RPG-Maker, or the really crappy sound effects. And if I have to point out something positive, I'll say that the music is pretty decent.
But the story... It tries to hook you up in a plot of moral dilemmas and hard choices, about a young person out of luck, alone in the cold, uncaring world. But every time the game was about to catch me in it, a blatant change of tone, terrible inconsistencies would break any immersion I was having.
The game tries to be dramatic and emotional, but any kind of tension is completely diluted by continuous 4th wall breakings, silly jokes and unnecessary collectables.
It also tries to sell you that your decisions matter, but they hardly do. For example, at one point, you might not have enough money to pay for a room, and find yourself sleeping in the streets. Which at first I thought it'd be terrible and a real handicap while trying to find a job and get back on my feet, turned to have absolutely no consequences.  You'd think that sleeping under the stars, among the hobos, not being able to take showers or change your clothes would have any negative effects in your health or social status, but no. You search for food in a trash can, heat it up in a burning barrel and sleep on a dirty mattress in a creepy alley, and then go to work as a top notch reporter in the local newspaper, then go dance at the expensive club at night. Just before you go back to sleep to your hobo alley. By the time I had enough money to rent a room, I didn't even consider doing it, because there was no point in doing so, at least, that I could see!
And on top of that, to get money, you have to do little mini games that are absolutely tedious. And I've played Papers, Please, and Cart Life, games that played on routine and struggling with your life every day, and enjoyed it. I couldn't keep playing Always Sometimes Monsters.

TLDR: Play as the goddamn Batman sneaking around Arkham Island punching bad guys in the face. Excellent story, game mechanics, and voice acting. All around awesome game.  9.5/10
Batman Arkham Asylum is one of the first great comic book games that I’ve played. In fact, the Arkham series is the only comic game series that springs to mind other than the various Spider-man games which were fun, but had serious technical problems. This game came out around the time of the second Christian Bale Batman movie, but has a completely different story and probably follows the comic / animated series much closer. But unlike in cartoons, people die in Arkham Asylum… a lot of them.
*Story spoilers*
When the game begins, Batman has captured Joker and is transporting him to the asylum on Arkham Island, where the criminally insane are kept separated from the people of Gotham City.  In a peculiar coincidence, a recent fire at the Blackgate prison in Gotham has caused hundreds of additional criminals to be temporarily housed in Arkham Asylum. So not only are there a bunch of super criminals (Killer Croc, Poison Ivy, Scarecrow, etc.) there’re also hundreds of Joker’s minions all in the same place. Of course it’s all a set up, and Joker is now exactly where he wants to be, king of the lunatics running the asylum.
Batman Arkham Asylum is played in the third person perspective on a relatively small “open world” map. You can probably run across the length of the island in less than 10 minutes, but a lot of the action takes place indoors (buildings bigger on the inside than outside). You can play Arkham Asylum like a stealth game for a lot of the encounters, but when it comes time to fight, the combat system is generally hand to hand punching, similar to Sleeping Dogs.  You have a utility belt full of tools and weapons but your greatest advantage in battle is the “counter” where you hit the counter button when you see an enemy about to attack, and Batman will automatically reverse the enemy attack and put the attacker in his place. This basically means that while you’re kicking and punching your enemies into submission, you are practically immune to damage if you always counter in time. There could be 20 bad guys and they wouldn’t touch you if you keep an eye on the attack warnings and have decent reflexes. Bosses are a different story though, and they add some variety to the mix.
Pros:
+Excellent story and voice acting, particularly for the Joker who is your main enemy taunting you from behind his army of thugs. A lot of familiar Batman enemies also show up to waylay you. The Scarecrow sections are probably my favorite story-wise.
+The combat and movement (gliding) mechanics are very well done. You can move through the maps with ease aided by your “detective mode” which is an augmented reality vision where you can see enemies through walls and detect interactive objects in the world. It’s kind of similar to the Thief 2014 “focus” or the Tomb Raider 2013 “survivor instinct.” The only drawback is that it turns your vision into a kind of x-ray type enhanced imaging, and you don’t see the well-drawn details of the world around you. I probably spent about half the game in detective mode.
Cons:
-Nothing really… unless you hate collecting objects after finishing a game’s campaign story. There are a ton of Riddler “puzzles” and collectibles to be found all over the island. By the time you finish the game’s story you will probably be about 50% complete according to the game’s progress meter. To get 100% you pretty much have to find every collectible and beat every “challenge map.”
Overall, Batman Arkham Asylum is a game everyone should play, if only to prove to yourself that awesome comic book video games are possible. Reccomending this game mostly to help boost it up to help it reach an audience. Most of what I can say about this game has already been said but if I could have one original idea it is to not be fooled by the people who are emphasizing the "high skill-ceiling" of the game, or "hardcore skill based" concept within that idea. It really isn't all what this community tries to eliticize it as (I made the word eliticize up). First of all, the "wow really high skill ceiling no shiters allowed" idea really shouldn't be a major selling point, it's more of a marketing point and a delusional vision if anything. Any game in the esports scene right now has an extremely high skill ceiling, and you know if someone has reached the potential peak of that ceiling if they have done all they can to be able to perfectly force the outcome in their favor. What that basically means is that in any of the highly competitive games to this day, no one has ever reached its "skill ceiling", examples are csgo, dota, league and games of those sort. However, it is completely useless to even mention considering the fact that there are countless games with depth, and along with that depth comes an untouchable skill ceiling. If you want an example of a real game with an actual low skill ceiling, it would be tic tac toe, anybody can easily reach the perfect play into either winning or tieing every single game. And above all else, why would any sort of skill ceiling matter when everything will come down to your own individual skill, you could play a game with a lower skill ceiling but why the ♥♥♥♥ would it matter when you probably won't ever reach that ceiling anyways, just focus on improving your self and don't focus on anything else. My point in all is that there is no reason to ever mention a skill ceiling when comparatively to other games, either no one or a few handful of people have ever reached that peak.
And just another point with the skill ceiling; Imagine all of the games out there either with somwhat of a competitive scene or an eports scene, and then think of the top players/teams among that scene. Yeah, they're insanely good and you'll probably never reach their level, you may think that that is the pinnacle of the game but then you realize those same players feel the same way as many of the players under them, they feel like they still can improve, some don't even think that they've reached their peak yet. And then if you have ever played a game with any ladder or ranked base system, you would know the lowest group within that system is utter♥♥♥♥♥♥ you would think anybody that plays in there has literally lost their mind. Brain Dead. So what makes lawbreakers any different? I ctrl f the word skill on the csgo page and it pops up 2x. ctrl f on quake live and it pops up 2x. ctrl f on rainbow six siege and it pops up 2x. Lawbreakers? ♥♥♥♥ing pops up 14x. The over obsession with skill in this game is ridiculous, the majority people I see talking about the skill in this game among the lb discord and steam are mostly all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥S. I've seen so many of the same thing said many times already, and they hold no truth when I actually play against these people. "lawbreakers will have less players because of the high skill ceiling and I like that, keep the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s out" "keep the kids out" "this is where skilled players actually play" Then why the ♥♥♥♥ is it when I play this game that many of those non ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ people are ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥ Why is it that it didn't take me long to start seeing and reach higher mmr players on the us west server (there's a hidden mmr system) and among those games, the players on the bottom of the scoreboard are all♥♥♥♥♥♥ And I've seen a lot of good players being in the high mmr specrum, but that didn't stop me from seeing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. The fact of the matter is that LawBreakers isn't any different, and that's why I mentioned the high end and low end skill groups in the beginning of the paragraph. Every competitive scene has a bell curve, there are the average, the incredibly low skilled, and the incredibly high skilled.
Now to the more arguable point of the game is it being skill based, and again it is over exaggerated and misunderstood but to bigger truth compared to the high skill ceiling argument, perhaps people are mistaking the two things. High skill ceiling is more of the difficulty in reaching the perfect form and play whilst a game being skill based is the idea of being rewarded for either team based or individual based skill with the lack of rng and other factors that require a low skill ceiling in order to take advantage of. This is practically the only thing worth talking about, as it contributes to a major selling point for myself, and that is if the game is a competitive shooter? Answer:Yes. And that would be all you would ever need to know, it is no use elaborating as much on that as I've had with talking about the skill ceiling of the game.
The game is skill based but is either overly exaggarated or emphasized to be so, especially with the contrasting implications of simply having a class/rolebased shooter on its hands. People were already trying to discover metas in the betas for christ sake, and there's nothing wrong with that as realistically its inevitable but it draws from how skill based the game will be so I don't have a ♥♥♥♥ing clue to how people are over exaggarating it. Actually, I do have a clue, and most of this elitism and hatred stems from the direct competition of overwatch. To say it is not is ♥♥♥♥ing stupid and there is an obviously blatant comparison when talking about skill of the game.
Should this game be compared to the likes of overwatch? YES. And I'm talking only about objective comparison, youtube comments give me cancer. Any game should be compared to a game that has some core similarities with it, this game should be compared to the likes of arena shooters as well, because comparison with different things brings out both original idea and more importantly, it talks about what actually matters. The graphics of the game, the optimization, the flow of rounds, the flow of mechanics, how objectives change the flow of the game, how map design changes the flow, what type of skills are required, does it have depth? To actually comparing the skill of both games, I'd rather not ruin the integrity of this review to talk about that, but to put shortly most of the comparisons made are utterly stupid to the fact that most players are either inexperienced or haven't reached an high understanding of competitive depth within games to even make a valid argument with actual knowledge. basically -people don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ they're talking about.
So yeah I lke the game, it is undeniably different and refreshing but I wouldn't call it revolutionary. The yearning for new experiences and feelings should be researched by every individual player because people have different experiences. And this review is part of that if anybody would to read it as a different perspective. What matters and appeals to me most about this game is:
What new concepts it brings to the plate:
To me the game brings a large cluster ♥♥♥♥ of ideas that have already been seen and puts it all in a mold, and so far with the resulting piece that has been put in front of me- I like it. What new things do I see in this game that I haven't experienced before? I like the gravity mechanic in the game, you can argue that its been done before already to which it is true, but the implication of it in lawbreakers brings a new dynamic which adds to both the movement and objective dynamics of the game to which I really like. At this point it's probably my favorite thing about LawBreakers and I would hope for the devs to bring up new ideas upon the movement mechanics.

So I came into this having loved TF2 and enjoyed overwatch, I was nervious because it could end up as another battleborn, but having played a couple of matches I realize that this game has all the things I missed from TF2, and all the bright sides of overwatch without some of the nagging negatives.
First off, after playing this I realized how heavily overwatch relies on lock-on and stun abilities, moba abilities, which are fine but not the best. This game requires aiming but doesn't require inhuman levels of practice to pull off moves.
Games also don't last too long, which is fantastic, the fighting is intense and action packed and matches have the possibility to last longer but on average they'll be about 5-10 minutes each.
I'd suggest this game to anyone who enjoys FPS games, the above mentioned in particular as well as older school FPS's like quake.

NOTE: I played this game when it was free, and I'm writing this before installing the game again, so some things may have changed while it was unavalible.
I have seen people call this an Overwatch clone, and I can see why they would think so. However, I think these games are different enough.
-Pros-
+GRAVITY. DEFYING. COMBAT. The low gravity can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥sometimes, but I still love it.
+The same classes on the different teams are different. They look different, sound different, but have the same weapons.
+I love the different classes. I love how they look (atleast most of them), move, shoot and everything else!
+The maps are very well made. A bit small, but fitting for all the current gamemodes. They are different, and there are not too many of them.
+The character/weapon skins look incredible. There are different rarities to the skins, and often the rarer they are, the better they look.
+I like all the current game modes.
+Each stash drop contains 4 items, so there's a bigger chance to get rare stuff.
+You get stash drops every time you level up, which in the beginning can happen like every match, but later
+It's incredibly fast-paced at times. While it can be pretty hard at first, once you learn it it becomes incredibly fun.
+Every character is different in almost every way. Some have secondary weapons, some can fly, some are melee etc.
+Except when I first join a new match, I experience very little lag
-Neutral-
*The character skins in one rarity usually look the same, but with different color schemes.
*There are not that many maps.
-Cons-
-Even though I like the gamemodes, most of them are pretty alike. You usually grab something from the middle and take it to a base.
-Too few gamemodes. I really want the casual CTF, TDM and some attack/defense.
-I usually lag a bit at the start of every match. It could be just me, and it doesn't last long, but it can be pretty annoying.
Overall, I REALLY encourage people to buy this game! 29.99$ will definetly be worth it!

It's like someone took Titanfall and Overwatch and smashed them together whilst also surgically removing tumors.
It's ridiculously fun. It's fast paced, but not TOO fast paced.
It's a hero shooter, but it's not TOO formulaic/meta.
Overwatch has a meta that can become boring, characters kill specific other characters everytime. People do the same things in the same part of the map every round. Lawbreakers doesn't have this. Every chracter can kill any other character if they're skilled. Every round is different because some of the objectives are LITERALLY JUST WIDE OPEN SPACES WHERE YOU CAN FLOAT. Support characters can kick♥♥♥♥♥too under the right circumstances, just like every other character. No matter what character you pick, you can always kick♥♥♥♥♥if you line up the kills right.
Titanfall was so fast paced that it became too chaotic, you never knew what was happening in a big gunfight. Titans could always beat specific other titan classes. People camped in the same buildings every round. You can't CAMP in lawbreakers because YOU'RE IN THE AIR. FLYING. FLOATING. DASHING.
Is it a hero shooter? Yes.
Do heros have ultimate abilities? Yes.
Do heros have specific jobs that they are meant to do? Yes.
BUT
Is it boring? No.
Is it an Overwatch copy? No.
Is it another TF2 wannabe? No.
It is an original, fast paced shooter with amazingly fun gameplay mechanics. You don't even have to pay $60 for it! The game is only $30! Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥that's a good deal!

In short, its TF2 x Tribes.
In long, if you've been looking for a game with more complex movement than spamming stafe keys and more complex tactics than going prone faster than your moth- well, lets just say its good, yeah?
As a short addendum, I've seen some people comparing it to Overwatch, which is honestly a pretty terrible comparison. L/B has a far higher emphasis on speed and personal skill than Overwatch, instead of Overwatch's high emphasis on team play and class choices.
So, final thoughts. Its good. If you like high movement speed and a lot of projectile based weaponry, go for it, its worth the buy, on or off sale.

So you know how when Overwatch was first coming out with gameplay footage and info, it looked like it would be really fun and engaging? Like a more updated Tf2?
Then it came out, and people realized it was slow, relatively unfun to play, and based more around the incredibly overpowered ultimate abilities rather than the actual gunplay.
Well Lawbreakers takes that dynamic and flips it onto its head. Everything about this game is built from the ground up to be satisfying.
The abilities of the characters make sense and are actually well integrated. Many characters can use abilities while firing their weapons, making the abilities feel more natural and less like poorly integrated side moves for specific situations.
None of the abilities are unfun either. There's no get out of jail free cards. No instant team wipe cc ults. No reflection, invisibility, or invincibility. In fact, nine times out of ten, the abilities are either movement based or damage based meaning the characters were built with the core gameplay values in mind. "Movement and damage"
The game modes reflect this. Blitzball is the most fun, as it revolves around grabbing the morty ball and bringing it to the enemy teams base. Since there isn't any character abilities that are blatantly unfair for this (Like an instant activated ghost form that allows players to move around without taking damage) this actually feels like a fun and intuitive mode.
The antigrav combat feels very natural. (For most characters at least, some feel a little bit too floaty, like Wraith). And because the main objective is usually in an antigrave arena, it feels like there is some strategy to the characters that one should pick. Obviously the best characters for the grav fields are the ones with rifles that work at long range and the ones with solid movement abilities for the air. This means it's gonna be Harrier, Enforcer, and Vanguard dominating the area with a good gunslinger picking out the straglers from the edges. This means that depending on the mode, and the objective, characters will get varied use. It's pretty refreshing to see this kind of thing.
I do have a few issues with a couple of the things in the game.
-Battery and uplink are the practically the same game mode. We don't need both.
-Battlemedic feels a little unfun when you're trying to take down his shield. I mean it's not egregious but I did notice that it was really strong. Maybe it's fine though since the cooldown is 6 seconds and I only saw the heals thrown out once in a blue moon anyway.
-Juggernaut can wall off the Blitz goal on certain maps. This kind of thing worries me for the games future, since even though it is counterable, it's the kind of strategy that might make juggernaut camping a staple of blitzball with little reprieve in the future.
Anyway that's my review. I love this game. Buy it.

I'm editing this review since it's a lot more viewed than I thought it would be. I'll try to break it up into objective and subjective parts.
OBJECTIVE (as much as possible)
Overall - 6/10
The content that is in the game is well done for the most part, but there's only 4ish maps and 4ish game modes, with two of the game modes (conduit and uplink) being very similar.
Graphics - 8/10
The unreal engine is used to full effect in this game, with character models sporting a good amount of detail and animations being on point for the most part. The only complaints I've had so far are some abilities are kinda lackluster, the titan's berserk for example, and the skin and hair shaders seem off although that could be my settings. Maps, pickups, weapons are all well done but I've had some strage graphical issues where random geometry will pop up while leaving the spawn or reloading or something.
Sound - 9/10
I don't usually pay attention to sound in games, but LawBreakers has some great audio. The background dubstep music is good for getting pumped up during a match and ability cues are usually audible. It can get a bit messy when a bunch of abilities are being activated or during blitzball when everyones favorite announcer starts yelling.
Gameplay - 7/10
I'll try to be as objective as possible. For the most part the gameplay works well. Characters take some getting used to but overall control relatively well. The disparity in movement options can be frustrating, with assassins, medics, wraiths, and mavericks being able to go wherever they want while other classes are a lot more limited in their movement. The Zero-G combat is definitely a nice new take on typical fps combat and can feel both great and extremely frustrating. With how twitchy the controls can be, it can be a real struggle to track enemies as they zip around and it's a bit too easy to get ganked from behind when you're trying to fight someone. Obviously this could be remedied with good teamwork, but most people so far haven't done much communicating during matches.
The game modes and classes both need some work. A lot of the game modes are fun but conduit, where both teams are trying to control and charge a single battery, can be a bit frustrating. If one team charges it to 100%, the other team can steal it at the last second and get the win. This sounds like it would create some interesting gameplay, and it does, but the flaw I found was that there's a 10 - 20 second cooldown on being able to steal the battery back. This means if your battery is stolen at 100%, and the other team gets it to their base you literally can't take it back and win. This causes more annoying plays like people playing the jet-fighter like maverick and just swooping in at the last second to steal the battery. I gave that long winded explanation as a way to highlight that while the game/game modes feel good overall there are some quirks that I think are more flaws than features.
Classes all feel interesting and unique, I'll illustrate my personal feelings on them below. With the ability to change classes mid match it's important to keep your team setup to counter the enemy effectively. Again since most people in matchmaking don't communicate this doesn't happen very often. I'm not sure what else I can add here without imparting too much opinion so I'll leave it at that.
SUBJECTIVE
Since people seem very sensitive to criticism about games and try to equate reviewers opinions with facts I decided to separate my opinion from what I felt was objective as much as possible. I really want to like the game, but I don't feel in control very often. What I mean by that is when I die, it tends to be because a wraith has snuck behind our team and 1-hits me or there's a bunch of titan rockets being shot down a hall and now I'm stuck in place. Admittedly I've given up playing twitch shooters back with CoD ghosts. It's the same reason I hate Overwatch, whoever can twitch and react faster wins, it doesn't feel like skill just reaction speed.
Classes -
Titan - I personally really don't like the titan. Your movement options are a damaging leap thats on a cooldown and rocket jumping. With all the other classes sporting such high mobility your rocket launcher can feel like a crap shoot unless you're shooting into a room or objective or something. Also, while good, the titan's ult just looks/feels really uninspired and cheesy to me.
Maverick - The jetpack, minigun sporting class. They feel like a lot of fun, zipping around with a minigun and all. The downside is your jetpack mode is really quick and you'll probably have some trouble trying to maintain aim with your cannon while using it. Also, the minigun fire rate and accuracy go up as you fire. This means that you won't be able to hit a barn wall until you've eaten a bit into your clip. Overall, this class feels good, but really shines in blitzball and conduit/uplink.
Harrier - Lasers, lasers everywhere. Harriers can be fun to play, and they're one of the easier classes to get damage with since you can just spray your constant laser beam all over the place. I'm sure there's a skill level required to be good with harriers, but most of the time they'll just hover near a battle firing their lasers into the mix. Always feels bad to be killed by one since their primary doens't feel very skillful.
Gunslinger - My personal favorite, so I'm a bit biased. Their primary is borderline useless unless your target is a couple feet away, but their Omega revolver is a straight up sniper rifle and has the damage to match. They're quite mobile with a teleport that has 3 charges that recharge over time. Fun and requires skill to be good. Their ult is a bit facerolly but eh, can't win it all.
Medic - I enjoy the medic, although if the enemy team is decent they'll just focus you down and you'll get gibbed just for leaving the spawn. Healing is handled well with a fire and forget system and their grenade launcher is interesting if a little like the titan's launcher in that it's really best for firing into objectives or indoors.
Assassin - A lot of fun, if a bit frustrating to use. They have a grapple that allows them to zip around the battle field and it's fun as hell to use. That being said, you can grapple players and reel into them to start a melee combo. This sounds great, but with the high mobility on most characters you'll (at least I did) quickly get disoriented and lose track of your target when you get into them. If you can sneak up behind someone and hit em a few times in the back, they'll go down, but trying to really fight people can be quite frustrating.
Wraith - Ef this class. This has been my biggest complaint so far. They come in as MVP in about 60%+ of the matches I've played and it's easy to see why. They can triple jump, wall jump, and slide for mobility. This allows them to dart back and forth and makes them a huge pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to try to track to kill. On top of their mobility they're probably one of the best burst classes in the game, especially if they can get their knife shot off and shoot it for the explosion follow up. With how many paths there are in most maps, you'll generally have a wraith running around behind your team stabbing everyone in the back. I take issue with pretty much being insta-gibbed if they get close. There's no warning and all of a sudden you're dead unless you're a titan or juggernaut.
I haven't played the other classes enough to comment yet.

TI;DR at bottom
So I'm reviewing this to help prespective new players wrap their minds around the whole dash drama. Dash if fine; in fact, it's great. If you didn't know already, for a very long time the only diffensive option was dodge. Initially it was simple, you would get a directional dodge in any direction with a 1 second cooldown on ground and 3 seconds in the air. That was a long time ago. The problem with this was that it gave passive players a much greater advantage over those trying to push in. Any and all approaches were slow and reactable, and you could easily play and win by keeping your distance and solely attack to punish an approach. The neutral game was rather trash. BMG (Blue Mammoth Games) did their best to try an alleviate this issue without massively shuffling mechanics. In the end Dodge became weird and convoluted; If you had enough forward momentum youcould speed dodge, which would be cancelable into an attack, you could dodge again on the ground to extend your current dodge, and you could (and still can, actually) preform an immediate speed dodge after landing an attack. But none of these things really fixed the core issue; all approaches were slow and reactable. So in favor of this new dash, directional dodges on the ground were completely removed; Inputting a direction (left or right) and pressing the dodge key will now preform a dash. This dash can be preformed at any time on the ground and has massive, instant acceleration and speed compared to anyhting else in the game at the time, but you won't have any invincibilty frames. This effectively made unreactable approaches a thing and the neutral game was much faster and intense. However, many people, myself included, had been playing with the old dodge for years now. I personally hadn't had too much of an issue with passive play and kinda felt that dodge was a bit unnecessary. But after having played it with my friends for a bit and then trying to go back to the old dodge, it felt much, much slower. The game as a whole feels much nicer; standing still and waiting for an attack is still a valid thing to do, but it involves more risk than it ever did, and you have to rely on your ability to read your opponent rather than simple reactions to pull it off. It took me anout a week or two to really adapt, and the game as a whole will be much more intuitive for a new player.
TL;DR: People got too comfortable with the old dodge and are now immaturely crying abt it and giving this game bad reviews that it absolutely does not deserve. Please don't let that drive you away from this game. If you ARE one of these people, please look into actually using dash before potenially ruining this game's only marketing source.

After playing Deus Ex Human Revolution (Predecessor of Mankind Divided) multiple times, being one of my favorite games, I looked forward to Mankind Divided. In short, Human Revolution a game with multiple paths and options, with a great storyline of conspiracy which you have to discover and uncover yourself. You can really invest yourself into the story.
The start of the game was, in my opinion, one of the weak parts: you're dropped right into contact with multiple characters and situations of whom you've never heard of before (except in the trailers), but whom are apparently well known to the main protagonist. While these connections were introduced rather sloppy, you do get to know them about two hours in.
The storyline overall is very good. The feeling of being kept in the dark was fun, as it led to many surprises to which you can react. The main story changed the rest of the universe as well, which makes you feel like you are really making an impact on it. The story connected to the previous games as well (With Human Revolution being the past and the original Deus Ex as the future) in a way that made sense. Multiple sidequests with connection to Adam Jensen, being old aquaintances or connected to the atmosphere and his opinion about them. Some sidequests are randomly found, which made solving those mysteries much more enjoyable.
The atmosphere of the game is great, you see the division of "Naturals" and "Augs" and the results because of it everywhere around you. The main protagonist can also strike up multiple conversations on the workfloor with colleagues, which made them feel like more than just random NPC's by having discussions or building up friendship even if it doesn't alter the storyline at all.
The combat has been vastly improved; in Human Revolution the normal pistol was an unchallenged king out of the other weapons, but in Mankind Divided each weapon has their own merit (Some large open fields for the sniper rifle, different types of special ammunition, effective range and piercing, etc). Gunfights have more glasscannon than bullet sponge enemies, which is something I enjoy as well. Adam's health felt quite low, but I haven't tried out the Titan shields yet, which should give Adam Jensen a much higher survivability. Some situations felt poorly planned, some ambushed start you in a 3v1 situation without cover, making it hard to find cover or take them out fast enough on the highest difficulties.
The stealth system was improved as well with multiple phases like panic, hostile and searching. Although this was already present in the predecessor, it's more fleshed out in Mankind Divided by making the stages of NPC's known from the start. The ability to pull enemies with you behind cover in hand to hand combat also was a quality of life improvement, making the game react more to your intentions (Because you almost always want to hide bodies).
The amount of possible paths to locations was even bigger than in Human Revolution, making every playstyle viable instead of a choice between vents and following the main path; almost every floor was a new maze of possibilities.
The cityhub felt a little less diverse than Human Revolution which had a wider variety of scenery with Hengsha and Detroit, as Mankind Divided only has Prague and a small moment in Golem City. It was, however, much more impressive than it's predecessor as the area's changed much more because of new events. Shops are all over the city, which made selling items and buying new ones quite easy. Shop interaction was kind of flawed; you have to sit through 4 one-liners of the NPC which narrow down to "I sell items. Please buy items?" before you get access to their computer (which contains their wares), and exiting wants you to confirm your exiting multiple times.
There is only one bossfight in Mankind Divided compared to Human Revolution's multiple, but it doesn't feel like this game is lacking them.
TL;DR:
Atmosphere feels rich and is vastly visible.
Combat and stealth is improved and feels great with multiple options.
Storyline is good, albeit the earlygame connection is weak.
Possible paths have increased tremendously, making even more playstyles viable.
It's a great game, a worthy successor of the earlier Deus Ex franchise.

It took me about 36 hours to complete the main story, I believe I did most of the sidequests.
There are a lot of issues, small and big, but the story is not one, IMO. A realistic depiction of what happens if a group of people is being made The Enemy, I had to reload several times because I just HAD to punch that civilian or policeman in the face (which meant I was instantly attacked from all sides, of course...)
I'm pleasantly surprised by the end video - instead of being a pre-defined block of video, it actually responds to what you did in-game. If you killed a person, it will be mentioned that he's dead. If you spared them, you are informed that they are in custody.
I was less pleasantly surprised by the end of the game itself - it's not exactly a cliffhanger, the immediate story is assumed completed, but there is a jump of two weeks just after you're going after the bad guys.
(Obviously, you won.)
That could have been handled better, and indeed maybe there was some content cut away.
One of the major grievances I have with the game is that the sidequests, or optional sub-quests are often confusing - either they're not listed until you failed to do them, or the quest directly leads you to a location that immediately precludes other options (i.e. you follow the message marker and are informed that you failed an optional, but NOT alternate, subquest - you could have done both!).
At least one sidequest was "expired" when I found it (I'm not sure how I should have found it, usually side-quests are announced, one way or another).
(Expired = I got it, I went there, nothing to do anymore, quest complete.)
A minor grievance is that too much of the dialogue, good as it is, is passive - all too often I had the feeling that I should have a way to steer the discussion.
A minor nitpick would be that in this game, as with HR, it is too easy not to kill. I gained the Pacifist achievement on my first playthrough - granted, I reloaded a lot, but there were hardly reasons to ever use the pistol, let alone any other weapon.
I'm not sure how this could be done better, though. Maybe give us a in-game reason why we'd want to actually KILL someone? (In HR, the only case where I actually felt that way was when Belltower massacred everyone in the Pod hotel. In MD, no one seems bad to enough to warrant that. Though a few certainly warranted a good punch on the nose...)
I had few minor issues in the game, loading times were mostly OK, EXCEPT for the train rides. For whatever reason, the system HAS to load for about 10 seconds - either the animation is fixed, or there is a LOT of loading and calculating. The game is on SSD, the OS is on a M2 SSD...
TL DR: Good game. If you enjoyed HR, you'll enjoy this.

As others said, it should have been integrated in the main game.
Aside from that, it's funny - shows a human side to Tarvos you don't really see otherwise.
Very short, of course, and the ending is rather abrupt - maybe they'll integrate it into the maingame once there is a Directors Cut, as they did with The Missing Link (which was far longer).

The marks will imbue you with power beyond any mortal, but there is a price to pay.  The legend tells of those that undergo the ink will do the will of the clan and then must turn their sword upon themselves or else bring ruin on their clan.  This story element really comes to fruition at the very end and was wonderfully put forward by the creators.  The story also comes alive with the fun and stylized are found through the game.
I would recomend the this game for those who have patience for stealth, and for everyone if it is on sale.

Brawlhalla is a great game.  I have been playing on and off since release and I have loved every minute of it.  There is such a depth and a variety of mechanics and strategy that make a fighting game so exciting that I can't put it down for more than a week.  With constant updates from the BMG team and an incredibly active community, I can safely say that this is the most fun and diverse fighting game out there.  Gamemodes include FFA brawl (4 players), a rotating custom game of some sort, and ranked (both 1v1 and 2v2).  There is also a training feature and an option to make a custom room for you and your friends.
Each of the 34+ characters feel so unique, be it the different equippable weapon combinations or the 6 unique signature moves each legend posesses, I gaurantee you'll find a hero that suits your playstyle.  Among many others, you've got a cowgirl, a gangster (think 50's mafia), and a straight up dragon.  The lore is somewhat whimsical yet very detailed, and the community is generally friendly and willing to give tips if you ask.
This game is still in open access and is entirely free to play, the only thing you need "real money" to purchase are skins and taunts, neither of which have any impact on the gameplay.  Occasionally, a new weapon or mechanic will be introduced, and some members of the community will take it upon themselves to ♥♥♥♥♥ and moan about how unfair the new weapon is, or how the new mechanic (dash being the latest) is going to RUIN THE GAME FOREVER!!!!1!!!  However, whether you're a fighting game veteran or totally new to the scene, you'll definitely find hours of enjoyment in Brawlhalla.
TLDR:
+Deep, varied mechhanics
+Smooth controls
+Reliable servers
+Constantly updated, active community
+Lots of characters to choose from
+/-Learning curve

This was the game that tied it all together.
Gameplay-wise, I won't say it's the best of the series, but on a technical level it was somewhat groundbreaking in bringing us into the world of multiple-opponent combat in its genre.  One of the big things they advertised about this game when it first came out was the ability to fight a crowd as a crowd, not let each one politely come up and get beat up when it's his or her turn.
Story-wise, this tied up so many loose ends in the series, and really made the story into what it should have been all along.  Follow with me: The first Blood Omen felt like a one-off, a Playstation game that was kindof fun but wasn't really going anywhere.  It was an overhead RPG-ish thing where you played as a vampire avenging his murder, and it made that into a bigger picture story where he was the victim of a greater plot.  Then Soul Reaver came out, with its awkward camera angles hat nearly made the game unplayable, block puzzles that nearly finished what the camera failed to do, and where someone in their infinite wisdom decided that the Soul Reaver story needed to be cut in half to sell two games instead of one.  I remember people dug into the disk and found content that was designed for continuing the story, but was unavailable in the game because they wanted you to play a second Soul Reaver.  Then Soul Reaver 2 and Blood Omen 2 were released, with massively improved gameplay mechanics and graphics.  The PS2 days.  Blood Omen 2 was a little hokey for backfill, but backfill it did, and it added more substance to the Vorador and Janos characters.  Soul Reaver 2 became more about tying the series together, and Raziel was less consumed with simply killing his maker as he learned more about the plot that entangled them all.  And for all the mind♥♥♥♥ that the time streamer's games had played on the antiheros and the player, Defiance really brought us back in full 3D amazingness to the intro video and the events from that first Blood Omen.  This is the game that tied it all together, and it did so in such a way that it made me love the entire series all over again.  Questions I didn't know I should ask, like why did the guardian fail to protect the circle, and from whom, were replayed and answered at the same time.  Just...  brilliant.
Also, the voice acting pretty much made this series, as much as the game itself did.  Simon Templeman is a total badass.
Last note; I played this through several times on PS2, and its predecessors once-to-four-times through on their respective Sony systems.  Steam made me load it up for five minutes to review, but I've played it though more than once.  My review is on the game itself, and I didn't include any technical details (OS, system hardware/performance).

EDGE is a tricky game to put labels on due to its unique mechanic: the player controls a cube which moves by flipping itself on its side, and can climb by grabbing ledges and flipping itself up, but cannot jump or attack or do much of anything else.  The cube is navigated through isometric 3D levels full of moving platforms while looking for collectible crystals, and eventually the exit.  It feels very old-school in its simplicity, harkening back to the computer games of the early 80's when there was no story or special abilities or even much of a point to playing at all, they were just sort of "there".  Levels are numerous, well-designed, and offer impressive variety in styles for the lack of gimmicks the game uses.  The isometric view can get tricky at times since navigation is still done with the arrow keys and the camera is not adjustable, but when combined with the cubic visuals it is truly an enchanting minimalist sight.  For a no-frills gameplay-focused experience that tackles things from a old angle that's new again, give EDGE a try.

That the game resets you back to just before you died also gets annoying fast, as at that point you usually have no choice but to restart (why isn't that the default?).
I can't say much of later levels, but the early ones had pretty unintuitive solutions to them either. I never had a "oooh, so THAT was what I was doing wrong!" moment when I looked up an answer. Rather, I felt that the only way to beat this game was to program something to just go with every possible combination of movements and let it run for some hours. Mark of the Ninja is an aesthetically pleasing, 2-D, stealth-based, side-scrolling platformer...a.k.a. a masterpiece. For those of you who want a brief overview without looking at it in the steam store, think of it as combining the best qualities of Thief, Dishonored, and Assassin's Creed and giving it all to you in a different, albeit wonderful, 2-D perspective.
To give you a sense of the story itself, you play as a ninja (no way, right?) who accepts the "First Mark," a tattoo which imbues mystical powers to the one who accepts it upon their body. While this seems like a fantastic benefit, accepting the mark means sacrificing yourself in the future because the ink is said to drive people to insanity (e.g., hallucinations). Your purpose-without spoilers-is to avenge your clan that was recently attacked by an evil arms corporation by utilizing your newly-acquired powers. As the story progresses, you receive more marks, more abilities, and more means to uncover the irreconcilable truth about your role, your clan itself, and those of power who essentially mean to save and/or destroy it.
Now if this hasn't already got you hooked or clicking off of my review to go buy it, then please allow me to further elaborate the feel of the gameplay. Mark of the Ninja does not care precisely how you play the game...to a certain extent. Yes, the stealth aspect is a given. This is not simply because this is the major theme/tag for the game itself (who knew?), but also because while you can dish out hits, you can't take many more hits than other enemies in the game. This is exceedingly true if you try to go in "weapons blazing" (expect to be punished and killed relentlessly if you do this). Despite this sometimes perceived "limitation" by some players, there are multiple routes and means of accomplishing each level through various stealth-based tactics. You can choose to be cruel, fast, and terrorizing, or merciful, meticulous, and tactful--or even a mix of these depending on the situation/your mood at any given moment! That's one of the most glorious aspects of the game: Freedom of choice to accomplish objectives. Combine this with the gorgeous settings for each level, and the 2-D game does not feel at all linear or dimensionally flat.
Finally, there are a couple of minor details I'd like to state that may or may not apply to other players (skip this if you like):
1) I admit that I played this game on steam with an Xbox 360 controller and not with the keyboard and mouse. I recommend doing so for the sake of the ease of controls. However, you may have your own preferences and be able to get used to keyboard/mouse controls faster in comparison to me.
2) At some points my computer lagged terribly due to how many various processes were going on in the game with the visual effects (e.g., when there was a raging sandstorm in one level). The creators even comment upon this minor flaw if you turn on the in-game commentary within the game itself (which I also recommend because it reveals some really awesome facets of the making of the game!).
3) Mark of the Ninja is a highly addictive game with major replay value. It took me 14 hours to complete it the first time through, and I intend on replaying it once again on new game+ mode in the future.
Hopefully, all of the aforementioned reasons will sway you to spend some money in steam to purchase a game that has certainly left its "mark" on me. Please don't think me insane for adamantly urging you to acquire this game instead of letting it sneak past some gamers unnoticed. I recommend picking it up immediately, but if you want to wait until it goes on sale in the steam store that's fine too. I doubt it will let you down regardless :)
In short, Mark of the Ninja gets a well-deserved 10/10 (ninja) stars in my book, and I'd like to thank Klei Entertainment for allowing me to play through this utterly amazing story.

TL;DR Version: Lawbreakers is a really fast paced hero shooter with quite a few differences from Overwatch despite the comparisons people draw between them. It's a ton of fun and worth the price. Victory depends very heavily on how skilled you and your team are. If you liked Quake or Unreal Tournament, then you'll probably like this game.
If fast paced shooters aren't your thing, then just go ahead and ignore this game. If you love fast paced shooters with lots of action this game is a must buy. I had tons of fun in the beta and even now with the official release. Lawbreakers is a hero shooter with two teams, the Law and the Breakers. Each team has their own iteration of a specific class. For example: the Assassin on the Law team is a chick named Hellion. Her Breakers counterpart is another woman by the name of Kitsune. Both have the same abilities and weapons, but their personalities and lines are completely different. It's pretty much the same with all the other classes. Some are even opposite genders. The most fun aspect of this game is the Zero-G zones where you're flying around the map and can use your guns to propel yourself quickly towards your objective by just hitting the control key. Some classes do have thruster packs that you can use instead, but they have to recharge after awhile. The most fun part about the Zero-G zones is that you have to be more aware of your surroundings as there are far less places for you to run for cover and you're more exposed the higher up in the air you are. Now considering that this is a hero shooter, I'm sure you've probably already compared this to Overwatch, but let me say this. This game is far from what Overwatch is. Overwatch is mostly about working together as a team to get kills and completing the objective. Lawbreakers isn't like that. Lawbreakers is more about playing skillfully and completing the objective. Meaning using your class to the best of your abilities. Every class has an almost equal chance of winning a fight agaist the other. Meaning the squishy Wraith can take out the tanky Titan in seconds if the player playing as the Wraith has the skills to use the Wraith effectively. On the other hand, if the player playing the Titan knows how to deal with a Wraith at a distance or point blank range, then the Titan player can win against the Wraith player. It's not like Overwatch where a Mercy player using Mercy's pistol can never win against DVa's mech or Winston without any backup. Another difference is that Overwatch is a much slower paced game in comparison to Lawbreakers. You see Team Fortress 2 ? you see Overwatch ? Well it's kinda like it but with faster paced gameplay.
The game, whilst having left the early access state not long ago, is still in developpement and new maps, guns, modes, mercs, etc. will be added.
It's price is fairly cheap considering what it has to offer.
PROs
+ Good level design: there's always differents paths to navigate trough the maps (nice for flanking) but they're not complicated and you won't get lost that easy.
+ Classes are various but have common grounds with each other: they all can be suited for shorter range, more defensive, faster, and so on.
+  Each merc has his own set of skills and you can choose two of them at a time, they allow for tons of different playstyles to be played.
+ There's no microtransations at all: when you get at least 2 hours of playing you get a box that contains a random skin for the boxe's class, and it resets every 48 hours. You don't need to pay for anything to open it. You can sell the box or the skins if you want. Also, when you have a certain amount of skins of a certain quality or season, you can craft an accessory. Each couple of month, the boxe's season changes for a new one and the old stop from dropping. You can buy "DLC" but they're only paid merc's skins (only skins, no gameplay changes) and some are free.
CONs
- They're not enough players depending on your timezone, and you can find some empty servers.
- The netcode isn't that great and depending on what server you've connected to, you can get a pretty bad game because of ping.
- Not a lot of maps or gamemodes atm but it will change as the game is still in devlopment.

TL;DR Version: Lawbreakers is a really fast paced hero shooter with quite a few differences from Overwatch despite the comparisons people draw between them. It's a ton of fun and worth the price. Victory depends very heavily on how skilled you and your team are. If you liked Quake or Unreal Tournament, then you'll probably like this game.
If fast paced shooters aren't your thing, then just go ahead and ignore this game. If you love fast paced shooters with lots of action this game is a must buy. I had tons of fun in the beta and even now with the official release. Lawbreakers is a hero shooter with two teams, the Law and the Breakers. Each team has their own iteration of a specific class. For example: the Assassin on the Law team is a chick named Hellion. Her Breakers counterpart is another woman by the name of Kitsune. Both have the same abilities and weapons, but their personalities and lines are completely different. It's pretty much the same with all the other classes. Some are even opposite genders. The most fun aspect of this game is the Zero-G zones where you're flying around the map and can use your guns to propel yourself quickly towards your objective by just hitting the control key. Some classes do have thruster packs that you can use instead, but they have to recharge after awhile. The most fun part about the Zero-G zones is that you have to be more aware of your surroundings as there are far less places for you to run for cover and you're more exposed the higher up in the air you are. Now considering that this is a hero shooter, I'm sure you've probably already compared this to Overwatch, but let me say this. This game is far from what Overwatch is. Overwatch is mostly about working together as a team to get kills and completing the objective. Lawbreakers isn't like that. Lawbreakers is more about playing skillfully and completing the objective. Meaning using your class to the best of your abilities. Every class has an almost equal chance of winning a fight agaist the other. Meaning the squishy Wraith can take out the tanky Titan in seconds if the player playing as the Wraith has the skills to use the Wraith effectively. On the other hand, if the player playing the Titan knows how to deal with a Wraith at a distance or point blank range, then the Titan player can win against the Wraith player. It's not like Overwatch where a Mercy player using Mercy's pistol can never win against DVa's mech or Winston without any backup. Another difference is that Overwatch is a much slower paced game in comparison to Lawbreakers. That's not to say that Overwatch is a slow game, but the pacing in Lawbreakers is way higher because the time to kill is super low. Though not as low as CoD. Another differece between this game and Overwatch is that there is no need for a medic. The medic can come in handy in some modes. However, there are plenty of health stations for you to run to and heal up on your own. Just be aware you can't camp at the health stations because they are a good distance from the objective so you can't just poke your head out and take some pot shots and run back to heal up. Though, they're not far away enough that you would spend awhile try to get to them anyway. There aren't a ton of maps or game modes yet, but considering this game is only $29.99 USD, this game is pretty worth it for what you're given. I've also heard the game will also recieve free dlc as well later on. Anyway, Lawbreakers is a ton of fun and I highly recommend it to anyone that loves fast paced shooters like this. I've also heard from quite a few people that if you ever played Quake or Unreal Tournament, then you'll probably like this game.

I've sunk about 25 hours into the game across the last three betas and today's release, and I love this game. If you like twitch shooters, lightspeed arena action, and plenty of movement options, you should absolutely buy this game. For those of who are unsure, or haven't been fragging since Quake's glory days, you should be aware that this game has a learning curve, and your probably going to take some lumps as you adjust to it. First off, go to the tutorials and watch them. Jump into private lobby and get a feel for the chracters and how the UI and game modes work first before you jump into a match. If you're too impatient to do all that, well, you really only have yourself to blame when your teams yells at you for not playing the objective.
You also need to be aware that LawBreakers is PvP only. No bots, the story is conveyed through descriptions of the characters and text boxes on the loading screen, and no horde mode equivalent.
Now, for the elephant in the room: Overwatch, and how they compare. I'll be blunt, the comparisons are superficial. Overwatch is character based, with each and every character behaving (somewhat) differently. LawBreakers is class based with a bit of extra pizzazz, and really has more in common with Quake or UT. Furthermore, LawBreakers is more balanced than Overwatch, with every class being perfectly viable provided you play to their strengths thanks to the fast movement and mixture of Zero Gravity zones. Also, no camping snipers or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t turrets here, though that's not to say LawBreakers doesn't have problems of its own. The Harrier is pretty dominant at the moment, as not many people know how to play around the newest class yet, and the Wraith is still really good in damn near every situation.
As for the maps... well, there are some really good ones, and there are some pretty terrible ones. Vertigo and Station are, frankly, pretty miserable to play on. Especially Vertigo, which has zero cover anywhere and the spawn points are right next to the objectives, making it trivially easy to defend against all but the most coordinated of assaults. Station has similar problems with every objective appearing in a tiny little murder-room in the middle of a 0-g area. Expect to run into gunslingers outside, and juggernauts inside, and be ready to get gibbed by both. That said, maps like Mammoth, Promenade, and Vertigo have none of those problems, and do excellent jobs of providing several routes into any objective from a myriad of angles while mixing up large open spaces with cramped corridors, all with plenty of cover.
As for the fun stuff, the skins and soundtrack are amazing! I would buy an album of LawBreakers' soundtrack in a heartbeat, and even the most basic skins look damn good, with a nice mixture of classy and flashy with a color for every occaision. I also like how the game looks, but art design is more of a personal preference. I've heard some people complain about sillouhette reading, but honestly? It's not that hard. The differences are pretty damned obvious in all but the most hectic of firefights.
So, in conclusion? I'd give the game a solid 9/10
TL/DR Version?
Pros: Lightning fast movement, silky smooth gunplay, sick skins, sweet music, fun maps, no cartoony♥♥♥♥♥♥ 0g is great, rocket jumping, feels like a natural evolution of the Quake/UT formula, only $30, Bosskey has promised to support the game for free after realease with new maps, modes, and classes
Maybes: Has a bit of a learning curve, absolutely requires twitch reflexes and good aim, art design may not be for everybody, and Blitzball is a dunk-fest
Cons: Vertigo is a chore to play on, Harrier is pretty dominant right now, and there's only quick play. Ranked is coming though, it's just not out on release.

What can I say? It's the definitive Batman game and possibly one of the best comic book games ever made.
The writing is top-notch, and the fact they got a lot of the VAs and writers from TAS (largely considered one of the best adaptions of Batman ever made, animated or otherwise) really makes it feel like what TAS would've been if it had the freedom of a PG-13 rating instead of being limited to a hard G-Rating (or PG in the case of movies like Mask of the Phantasm.). The background stuff like the interview tapes and hidden messages from The Ghost of Arkham we're also great. This is one of the few games I felt compelled to gather all the other stuff in.
The gameplay is fluid and really captures the badass feeling playing Batman should entitle and gives you room to either be stealthy or go in swinging and fight everyone head-on with combat that feels satisfying and meaty due to the way the enemies react to hits and accompanying sounds of blows connecting and bones cracking.
The graphics and art-design are great and it runs at a near flawless and consistant 1080p/60FPS on my 750ti. I say near-flawless because there's one huge problem:
The implentmation of PhysX is horrid and the few areas that make heavy use of it suffer from severe FPS drops if you have it turned on.
The only two flaws I can really list aside from that tech failure (which is minor since there's only like three short levels it effects) are the somewhat lack-luster boss fights and the weird save-system that only really triggers when you go through a door seperating areas.

This is basically a stand-alone expansion of Far Cry 3. Without revealing too much, this game is a parody of 80's popular culture that plays almost exactly like Far Cry 3. It is gorgeous, it is funny, and, most importantly, it is fun. I would even go so far as to argue that it has slightly better replay value than the original Far Cry 3.
With the positives out of the way, here are the reasons why I am giving it the thumbs-down rating:
While I would argue that it has slightly better replay value than the original Far Cry 3, I would also argue that the lack of content kinda negates the increased replayability to some degree.
While I could tolerate the potential negatives of Uplay from a technical standpoint, the potential negatives from a business standpoint are enough by themselves for me to give a game a thumbs-down rating. What I'm talking about, to be more specific, is a Uplay feature unofficially referred to as "Steam Mode". When your Uplay library consists only of games bought through Steam, the store becomes inaccessible through the Uplay application. On top of that, many of the free games and demos/trials in the "Free Games" section of Uplay are removed. You have to make a purchase through Uplay in order to have these features reenabled. Sounds like an awfully slimy business tactic to me.
The game itself is good. Great, even. But the decision I have to make here is whether or not I would recommend people to spend their hard-earned cash on this product. Unfortunately, my answer is no.

Let's go over a simple list of pros and cons now that I've rambled.
Pros -
Graphics look great
The game sounds great
Smooth intuitive controls and gameplay flow
Versatile cast suited for variety of playstyles
Great variety of skins and customizables
Good variety of game modes
Online works fine, matchmaking can take some time but never too long, good netcode
Cons-
Not many maps yet
If you don't like lootboxes, sorry but this game has them
Beta community was toxic as hell (though that may have been because it was free) haven't noticed this issue since launch however.
